# Smarter Crowdsourcing in the Age of Coronavirus

[![Smarter Crowdsourcing | Zika Logo](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/images/coronavirus-logo.png)](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/)

### Imagine if epidemiologists, computer scientists, urban planners, policymakers and those with diverse know-how could talk to one another to design actionable solutions to fight Coronavirus

### Imagine if the smartest and most innovative people could come together to build the Coronavirus strategic preparedness and response quickly and easily

### Imagine if epidemiologists, computer scientists, urban planners, policymakers and those with diverse know-how could talk to one another to design actionable solutions to fight Coronavirus

Complex and interdependent problems, like coronavirus, demand access to expertise that is widely dispersed. Global and complex public health emergencies threaten public health and well-being, risk disruption to global and regional trade and economic stability, and cause widespread uncertainty and concern. This project will focus on devising innovative solutions to public health challenges across all four stages of crisis response, including mitigation, preparedness, response and recovery.

# About Smarter Crowdsourcing in the Age of Coronavirus

## About

## ABOUT THE PROJECT

Complex and interdependent problems, like coronavirus, demand access to expertise that is widely dispersed. Global and complex public health emergencies threaten public health and well-being, risk disruption to global and regional trade and economic stability, and cause widespread uncertainty and concern. This project will focus on devising innovative solutions to public health challenges across all four stages of crisis response, including mitigation, preparedness, response and recovery.

## ABOUT THE GOVLAB

[www.thegovlab.org](http://thegovlab.org/)

The GovLab is an action research center based at the Tandon School of Engineering at New York University. Our mission is to improve people’s lives by changing the way we govern. Our goal is to strengthen the ability of institutions – including but not limited to governments – and people to work more openly, collaboratively, effectively and legitimately to make better decisions and solve public problems. We believe that increased availability and use of data, new ways to leverage the capacity, intelligence, and expertise of people in the problem-solving process, combined with new advances in technology and science can transform governance. We approach each challenge and opportunity in an interdisciplinary, collaborative way, irrespective of the problem, sector, geography and level of government.

## ABOUT THE INTER-AMERICAN DEVELOPMENT BANK

[www.iadb.org](http://iadb.org/)

The Inter-American Development Bank is an international financial institution whose goal is to improve the quality of life of people in Latin America and the Caribbean by financing economic, social and institutional development projects and promoting regional economic integration.

# Recommendations

Recommendations for governments to strengthen government capacity for COVID testing strategies, contact tracing programs, public health communications, vulnerable population supports, monitoring systems, and mental health interventions

The outcomes of this project are a set of [18 recommendations](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/recommendations) developed with the support of global experts. These recommendations are designed for government officials to aid them as they address the COVID-19 pandemic. Each recommendation is supported by [a set of strategies](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/strategies) to achieve that recommendation. Strategies in turn detail actions and global examples that guide governments of the specific steps needed for implementing the strategy.

[EXPLORE THE RECOMMENDATIONS](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/recommendations#recco) [EXPLORE THE STRATEGIES](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/strategies)

## Recommendations

[

Pooled Testing

Governments and researchers should implement pooled testing strategies, innovating with pool design through ranking schemes or geographic schemes.

](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/recommendations/pooled-testing)

[

National Patient Identifiers

Governments should take steps toward developing a unique health identifier/national patient identifier system (UHI/NPI) that unambiguously identifies each individual and links her to her health records, including test results.

](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/recommendations/national-patient-identifiers)

[

High-risk populations

Governments should prioritize conducting tests among populations with a high probability of 1) contracting the virus; 2), spreading it to others; and 3) suffering serious consequences as a result of infection.

](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/recommendations/high-risk-populations)

[

Metrics

Governments should establish and use metrics to (1) indicate thresholds where contact tracing is more or less effective as a containment and mitigation strategy; and (2) track progress and effectiveness of ongoing contact tracing programs.

](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/recommendations/metrics)

[

Interjurisdictional Coordination

Governments should increase vertical and horizontal interjurisdictional coordination by (1) incentivizing the use of interoperable or the same contact tracing platform and data collection process and (2) creating opportunities for knowledge sharing.

](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/recommendations/interjurisdictional-coordination)

[

Localization

Governments should increase public trust in contact tracing programs by ensuring the programs incorporate local knowledge and experience. Specifically, they should (1) conduct an assessment that identifies community assets; (2) partner with local community organizations to identify contact tracers; (3) conduct a public health messaging campaign to explain contact tracing; and (4) incorporate information about the local community when training the contact tracing workforce.

](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/recommendations/localization)

[

Improve Data Management

Improve data management (collection, storage, and analysis) processes to support evidence-driven programs and policies that identify vulnerable populations and account for their needs.

](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/recommendations/improve-data-management)

[

Establish Public-Private Partnerships

Establish Public-Private Partnerships that support vulnerable populations by filling service delivery gaps that community-based organizations, governments, and NGOs struggle to execute efficiently working on their own, while also benefiting the private institutions by providing them with financing and other resources.

](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/recommendations/establish-public-private-partnerships)

[

Engage the Public and Civil Society Organizations

Engage the public and civil society organizations to support vulnerable populations by capitalizing on existing knowledge and expertise, leveraging local assets and resources, building trust with intended beneficiaries, and strengthening the capacity of communities.

](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/recommendations/engage-the-public-and-civil-society-organizations)

[

Enhance Data Collection

Enhance data collection capabilities through innovations in technologies, crowdsourcing, symptom-trackers, and partnerships.

](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/recommendations/enhance-data-collection)

[

Improve Information Infrastructure

Improve public health monitoring and surveillance information infrastructure by standardizing data formats and definitions, sharing data, and developing regulations and legislation that support public health monitoring and surveillance.

](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/recommendations/improve-information-infrastructure)

[

Increase Government Capacity

Increase government capacity to use public health monitoring and surveillance information to make policy and programmatic decisions.

](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/recommendations/increase-government-capacity)

[

Government capacity and regulatory environment

Improve legislative and regulatory frameworks for mental health services.

](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/recommendations/government-capacity-and-regulatory-environment)

[

Data and Technology

Use digital technologies and data to and expand access to mental health services and improve service delivery.

](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/recommendations/data-and-technology)

[

Increase provider capacity

Increase provider capacity through innovations in training opportunities and strategies to expand the workforce supply.

](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/recommendations/increase-provider-capacity)

[

Evidence and misinformation

Combat misinformation through evidence-based, clear, and consistent messaging.

](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/recommendations/evidence-and-misinformation)

[

Community and stakeholder engagement

Engage communities and other stakeholders to make messaging strategies context specific and culturally relevant.

](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/recommendations/community-and-stakeholder-engagement)

[

Data and innovation

Use data and innovations like crowdsourcing to optimize messaging development, reach, and uptake.

](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/recommendations/data-and-innovation)

# Strategies

Strategies for implementing recommendations proposed by experts through Smarter Crowdsourcing conferences

The outcomes of this project are a set of [18 recommendations](http://localhost:8000/recommendations.html) developed with the support of global experts. These recommendations are designed for government officials to aid them as they address the COVID-19 pandemic. Each recommendation is supported by [a set of strategies](http://localhost:8000/strategies.html)to achieve that recommendation. Strategies in turn detail actions and global examples that guide governments of the specific steps needed for implementing the strategy. Each strategy is a means to achieve a specific recommendation. You can explore individual strategies by searching by keywords, audience, type of strategy, and timeline.

[EXPLORE THE RECOMMENDATIONS](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/recommendations) EXPLORE THE STRATEGIES

## Strategies

TOTAL NUMBER OF STRATEGIES IN THE REPOSITORY: **73**

FILTERED STRATEGIES: **73**

### STRATEGY

### Topic

### RECOMMENDATION

[

Partner with academic institutions,researchers and private sector laboratories. Governments should engage the academy,research firms,and private sector laboratories to develop algorithms,testing strategies,and innovative ways to design pooled testing schemes.

Testing Strategy

Pooled Testing

](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/strategies/Partner-with-academic-institutions,researchers-and)[

Waive regulatory barriers. Governments should consider ways to adjust regulations that restrict innovation pertaining to pooled testing schemes.

Testing Strategy

Pooled Testing

](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/strategies/Waive-regulatory-barriers.-Governments-should-cons)

[Rapidly pilot pooled testing schemes. Governments should act quickly (<1 month) to pilot various pooled testing schemes such as Dorfman,Splitting,Sterret,and Matrix testing to gauge scalability and utility amongst](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/strategies/Rapidly-pilot-pooled-testing-schemes.-Governments-) [different contexts and populations](https://www.eurekalert.org/pub_releases/2020-04/su-vst042820.php).

Testing Strategy

Pooled Testing

[

Iterate learning and share best practices. Governments should contract with or perform their own evaluation of pooled testing schemes,improve on existing processes,and share best practices across jurisdictions and sectors.

Testing Strategy

Pooled Testing

](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/strategies/Iterate-learning-and-share-best-practices.-Governm)[

Conduct feasibility studies. Governments should appoint a group of government and external experts to conduct a feasibility study of jurisdictional and private/public context and document legislative opportunities or barriers to moving forward with a UHI/NPI system.

Testing Strategy

National Patient Identifiers

](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/strategies/Conduct-feasibility-studies.-Governments-should-ap)[

Standardize data entry fields across existing systems. Governments should work with partners to standardize data elements across health IT systems so that data is easily shareable between systems.

Testing Strategy

National Patient Identifiers

](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/strategies/Standardize-data-entry-fields-across-existing-syst)[

Develop,advocate for and pass legislation. Governments should mandate adoption of standards providing for a standard national health identifier for each individual,employer,health plan,and health care provider for use in the healthcare system.

Testing Strategy

National Patient Identifiers

](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/strategies/Develop,advocate-for-and-pass-legislation.-Governm)[

Adjust existing data collection processes. Governments should advance the use of regularly collected demographic data elements for patient matching and identification such as phone numbers,mailing addresses,or email addresses. This will ensure that public health authorities have up-to-date contact information when receiving reports from laboratories,hospitals,and other testing sites.

Testing Strategy

National Patient Identifiers

](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/strategies/Adjust-existing-data-collection-processes.-Governm)[

Establish a single organization to manage and oversee the UHI/NPI system. Governments should establish a single organization with the responsibility to oversee and advise on ways to improve patient matching and incorporate new technologies and approaches as they emerge. This organization would identify and encourage adoption of certain standards—such as on biometrics or use of smartphones—by health care organizations and technology developers.

Testing Strategy

National Patient Identifiers

](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/strategies/Establish-a-single-organization-to-manage-and-over)[

Implement a UHI/NPI system. Governments should roll out a comprehensive and single UHI/NPI system that integrates,delivers,and manages health information technology systems across all health care institutions,including the ability for individuals to access and control their own health records.

Testing Strategy

National Patient Identifiers

](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/strategies/Implement-a-UHI/NPI-system.-Governments-should-rol)[

Define high-risk populations who will receive prioritized testing. Governments should develop a working definition of which populations are high risk. Groups can be added to this list,but the list should identify populations that are at higher risk of contracting and having complications from COVID-19 due to physical health,behavioral health,or economic/social factors.

Testing Strategy

High-risk populations

](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/strategies/Define-high-risk-populations-who-will-receive-prio)[

Partner with community and cultural leaders. Governments should conduct specific outreach and form partnerships with community and cultural leaders to 1) understand needs and concerns of specific communities and 2) amplify public health messaging encouraging surveillance,diagnostic,and screening testing.

Testing Strategy

High-risk populations

](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/strategies/Partner-with-community-and-cultural-leaders.-Gover)[

Make testing free for low income or high-risk populations. Governments should reduce barriers to testing by making testing free for specific populations,ideally for screening or surveillance purposes.

Testing Strategy

High-risk populations

](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/strategies/Make-testing-free-for-low-income-or-high-risk-popu)[

Develop and use culturally and contextually relevant communication materials for testing resources. Governments and public health officials should make all communication materials targeted at high-risk or vulnerable populations accessible and culturally-relevant.

Testing Strategy

High-risk populations

](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/strategies/Develop-and-use-culturally-and-contextually-releva)[

Rapidly conduct snapshot pooled testing among staff and residents in health and long-term care facilities,prisons,and other congregate housing facilities. Governments should conduct snapshot pooled testing to provide a baseline that will help establish subsequent testing strategies within these settings,including the frequency of testing.

Testing Strategy

High-risk populations

](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/strategies/Rapidly-conduct-snapshot-pooled-testing-among-staf)[

Ensure adequate testing resources are available and accessible to high-risk communities. Governments should establish testing sites in communities with large numbers of high-risk individuals.

Testing Strategy

High-risk populations

](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/strategies/Ensure-adequate-testing-resources-are-available-an)[

Reduce barriers to testing by conducting mobile testing units. To address transportation limitations,non-traditional work schedules,and lack of access that may keep some communities from getting tested,governments should strategically implement mobile testing units that travel to vulnerable communities.

Testing Strategy

High-risk populations

](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/strategies/Reduce-barriers-to-testing-by-conducting-mobile-te)[

Make raw data available to researchers,public health professionals and epidemiologists. Governments should make disaggregated and,where appropriate,raw data available for modeling and epidemiological analysis. Sharing key process and outcome data with demographic and geographic identifiers allows researchers and public health officials to better predict and respond to the spread of the virus and emerging outbreaks.

Contact Tracing

Metrics

](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/strategies/Make-raw-data-available-to-researchers,public-heal)[

Incentivize adoption of standardized process and outcome measures within jurisdictions (vertical standardization) and across jurisdictions (horizontal standardization) through technical assistance and cost reimbursements or cost sharing. Governments should use legislative,regulatory,and budgetary means to incentivize and/or mandate the adoption of standardized metrics across jurisdictions.

Contact Tracing

Metrics

](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/strategies/Incentivize-adoption-of-standardized-process-and-o)[

Create and publish data dashboards that are updated regularly and show progress on metrics. Governments should develop a dashboard aligned with both the contact tracing platform and surveillance/reportable disease databases.

Contact Tracing

Metrics

](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/strategies/Create-and-publish-data-dashboards-that-are-update)[

Commit to carefully selected metrics that can be reported on consistently and regularly (do not select too many metrics). Governments should be cautious to select a small number of useful and informative metrics that can be reported on consistently,precisely,and accurately. Committing to too many metrics may lead to the inability to accurately and precisely track the data.

Contact Tracing

Metrics

](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/strategies/Commit-to-carefully-selected-metrics-that-can-be-r)[

Collaborate with private and public-sector actors that have large membership across jurisdictions. Governments should actively seek partnerships with businesses and organizations (e.g. unions) that have large numbers of employees or members based in various regions/states within the country. These businesses and organizations may be able to support interjurisdictional coordination.

Contact Tracing

Interjurisdictional Coordination

](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/strategies/Collaborate-with-private-and-public-sector-actors-)[

Use executive orders or other regulatory or legislative authorities to incentivize centralized platforms for contact tracing. Governments,ideally at the federal level,should mandate a single platform for contact tracing. If it is not possible at the federal level,governors of states/regions should mandate the use of a single platform within their jurisdiction.

Contact Tracing

Interjurisdictional Coordination

](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/strategies/Use-executive-orders-or-other-regulatory-or-legisl)[

Use legislative or regulatory mechanisms or executive orders to enable data sharing across jurisdictions. Governments should reduce the regulatory burdens that hinder or inhibit data sharing between jurisdictions.

Contact Tracing

Interjurisdictional Coordination

](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/strategies/Use-legislative-or-regulatory-mechanisms-or-execut)[

Use legislative or regulatory mechanisms or executive orders to enable agencies to share existing databases. Governments should capitalize on existing databases or registers maintained by specific government agencies (such as social security,post service,or census data) to bolster contact tracing efforts.

Contact Tracing

Interjurisdictional Coordination

](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/strategies/Use-legislative-or-regulatory-mechanisms-or-execut)[

Move towards a centralized communicable and reportable disease database and contact tracing capability. Governments should begin to invest in a federally centralized communicable and reportable disease database that will include contact tracing capabilities.

Contact Tracing

Interjurisdictional Coordination

](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/strategies/Move-towards-a-centralized-communicable-and-report)[

Offer informal peer learning opportunities. Governments or representative associations should coordinate informal forums or opportunities for individuals designing,implementing,and managing contact tracing programs to share ideas,challenges and best practices. These opportunities should be extended to include researchers,epidemiologists,or non-governmental actors with contact tracking experience.

Contact Tracing

Interjurisdictional Coordination

](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/strategies/Offer-informal-peer-learning-opportunities.-Govern)[

Offer formal peer learning opportunities. governments or representative associations should coordinate formal and structured forums or opportunities for those designing,implementing,and managing contact tracing programs to share ideas,challenges and best practices.

Contact Tracing

Interjurisdictional Coordination

](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/strategies/Offer-formal-peer-learning-opportunities.-governme)[

Create regional partnerships and coordinating bodies. Governments or representative associations should establish formal and informal groups and coordinating bodies based on regional or geographic similarities,such as transportation corridors or shared geographic borders.

Contact Tracing

Interjurisdictional Coordination

](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/strategies/Create-regional-partnerships-and-coordinating-bodi)[

Conduct a community health assessment that identifies community assets. Public health agencies responsible for conducting contact tracing should conduct an assessment of community organizations and assets that can be mobilized to support the contact tracing effort.

Contact Tracing

Localization

](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/strategies/Conduct-a-community-health-assessment-that-identif)[

Partner with local community organizations to recruit and hire contact tracers with community-based knowledge and experience. Governments should partner with local community organizations to identify contact tracers with the trust and knowledge of the local community. Selecting the right messenger is an important step to building trust,allowing for the cases and contacts to reveal details about who they have been in contact with and when.

Contact Tracing

Localization

](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/strategies/Partner-with-local-community-organizations-to-recr)[

Conduct a public health messaging campaign explaining contact tracing. Governments should perform outreach to the public with messages about contact tracing before and while they implement telephone and in-person interviews and contact tracing. This will help the public understand why they are being contacted and what the goal of these efforts are.

Contact Tracing

Localization

](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/strategies/Conduct-a-public-health-messaging-campaign-explain)[

Incorporate communication about contact tracing into the testing program. Testing centers should inform those who are tested that they will be contacted by someone from the contact tracing program if they test positive. The testing site should provide the name of the contact tracing program and the phone number from which people will receive a call.

Contact Tracing

Localization

](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/strategies/Incorporate-communication-about-contact-tracing-in)[

Incorporate information about the local community when training people for the contact tracing program. Governments and those designing contact tracing training programs should include specific modules that focus on the local community context,cultural practices,language considerations,and other specific considerations. The training program should also include information about how to conduct contact tracing,the workforce needs information about the local public health system,how it is organized and how it interacts with other agencies.

Contact Tracing

Evidence and misinformation

Data and innovation

](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/strategies/Governments-should-develop-strategies-for-testing-)[

Governments should understand the preferences of their constituencies and use tools that populations are most comfortable with. For example,live streams on social media platforms like facebook- which people use regularly and have fewer barriers to access-- tend to be more popular then webinars or conversations on platforms like Zoom or WebEx.

](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/strategies/Governments-should-understand-the-preferences-of-t)[

Data and innovation

Governments should analyze what physical barriers make it more difficult or increase the perceived effort of following preferred behaviors,and minimize or remove these barriers. The fewer steps and the less thought a preferred behavior requires,the more likely people are to follow it.

# Outcomes

[DOWNLOAD THE FINAL REPORT](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/files/SmarterCrowdsourcing_Report_EN.pdf) [DOWNLOAD THE EXECUTIVE MEMOS](https://directus.theburnescenter.org/assets/3e1b4334-472c-4770-a965-72590743daf0)

The outcomes of this project are a set of [18 recommendations](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/recommendations) developed with the support of global experts. These recommendations are designed for government officials to aid them as they address the COVID-19 pandemic. Each recommendation is supported by [a set of strategies](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/strategies) to achieve that recommendation. Strategies in turn detail actions and global examples that guide governments of the specific steps needed for implementing the strategy.

[EXPLORE THE RECOMMENDATIONS](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/recommendations) [EXPLORE THE STRATEGIES](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/strategies)

## About the products

To view these resources you can either (1) download the master report [(here)](http://localhost:8000/files/SmarterCrowdsourcing_Report_EN.pdf) which has all of the materials compiled into a single resource or (2) visit the advisory session page [(here)](http://localhost:8000/topics.html) where you can view resources grouped by the respective session topic.

### TITLE

### Description

### Use

[

Conference Materials

Problem Catalogue

Problem identification and prioritization is the first phase of the Smarter Crowdsourcing process. This problem catalogue document is a catalogue of possible core problems related to the pandemic complete with brief descriptions of each problem. The IDB used this collection of problems to select the six priority problems that became the six sessions of the Smarter Crowdsourcing project. Each selected problem was the subject of an online advisory session to identify good practices worldwide and distill significant learnings that can help to better understand how these initiatives can be reproduced in the region.

- Orientation to a scope of problems governments must address during the pandemic
- Menu that allows government to select specific problem and target resources

](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/files/sc_problem_catalogue_en.pdf)[

Conference Materials

Problem Brief

These **problem brief** documents provide a short description of the problem that each session sets out to solve. In addition, they include a rundown of root causes, an explanation of why the problem is important and compelling to solve, sample solutions and framing questions for the online advisory session.

- Background information on problem
- Framing questions for solution-oriented discussion

](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/topics)[

Conference Materials

Regional Report

These **regional reports**, one for each of the six advisory sessions,  contextualize the problem to the reality and situation in the partner and participating countries. The information is based on research as well as interviews with government representatives. The document highlights the concerns and specific questions that countries wanted answered/addressed.

- Country-specific contextualization of the identified problem
- Background information on country healthcare systems, public health infrastructure, and cultural context

](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/topics)[

Conference Materials

Participant Bios

For each online advisory session, the GovLab and the IDB identified and invited participants from diverse backgrounds who have the practical experience, subject matter and related data, tech or methods expertise and, above all, people who have demonstrated success solving the problem in the domain or a related domain. These **participant biography documents** list the biographies of those who participated in the advisory session.

- Menu of experts to consult for information and advice on potential solutions
- Introduction to network of researchers, practitioners, government officials, and private sector innovators

](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/topics)[

Conference Materials

Session Takeaways

Each **session takeaway** document is a summary of solutions proposed during each online advisory session. It is not a transcript. This document is used to invite participating governments to select which solutions are of greatest use to them and then develop those ideas into actionable proposals.

- Cursory list of innovative ideas to explore and develop further
- Foundation of recommendations and strategies in each recommendations memo

](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/topics)[

Conference Materials

Recommendations Memo

These **recommendation memos** are designed for government officials and civil servants who are interested in addressing the problem identified in the advisory session. Each document puts forth three recommendations on how to address the problem with accompanying implementation plans, examples, and experts to contact. The memos also incorporate considerations for governments trying to implement the recommendations as well as background information on the problem itself.

- Detailed recommendations and action plans directed at government officials
- List of examples, best practices, and experts to contact for further consultation

](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/topics)[

Final product

Executive Brief

These **high-level briefing documents** are designed for senior officials who do not need the level of detail in the recommendation memo. There is one brief for each of the six advisory sessions. Each briefing document contains a description of the topic/problem, recommendations for how to address the problem, strategies for implementing the recommendation, and examples of the strategies in action. The documents also contain resource estimates for the time and cost it may take to achieve  the recommendation as well as the estimated impact it will have if the recommendation is achieved.

- For individuals who need top-level recommendations but don’t need implementation details
- Complements recommendations memo as an executive summary.

](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/executive-memos)[

Final product

Master Report

This 300+ page **master report** includes a synthesized compilation of all the resources from the Smarter Crowdsouricng in the Age of Coronavirus Project. The document is broken into six chapters - one for each topic covered during the engagement: Testing Strategies, Contact Tracing, Behavioral Science, Vulnerable Populations, Monitoring and Surveillance, and Mental Health and Emotional Wellbeing. This document is available in English, Spanish, and Portugese.

- Resource manual consolidating all outputs from the project into a single document
- Detailed implementation plans for implementing partners/stakeholders

](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/files/SmarterCrowdsourcingCovid_Report.pdf)[Final product

Interactive Database of Solutions and Recommendations

The outcomes of this project are a set of 18 recommendations developed with the support of global experts. These recommendations are designed for government officials to aid them as they address the COVID-19 pandemic. Each recommendation is supported by a set of strategies to achieve that recommendation. Strategies in turn detail actions and global examples that guide governments of the specific steps needed for implementing the strategy. This **sortable and searchable catalogue** of all recommendations and strategies is available online and allows policy makers, researchers, government officials, and civil servants to explore the project and identify recommendations that are relevant to serving their constituencies.

- Online interactive resource listing all recommendations, strategies and actions from the project
- Searchable and sortable by topic, audience, resources, time, keywords, and stakeholders.](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/strategies)

# Testing Strategy

How do we design and source tests? How do we determine whom to test? What is the best strategy to administer tests and collect data?

[RECOMMENDATIONS MEMO](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1zKEiumAM1lKJBdijORviBacpkbE9Z63V5tHWq2f4nms/edit?usp=sharing) [CONFERENCE TAKEAWAYS](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1bVMfzHyIelGvaWA-oVnb9JqykmCqZ1-QqYOBm5blQxM/edit?usp=sharing)

## DESCRIPTION

We identify three categories of problems associated with testing. How should we design and source tests? This involves the challenge of how to increase the availability of testing and reliability of the existing tests. In addition to barriers associated with the supply chain, it is important to overcome political barriers to increasing testing when officials may not want to highlight the size of the problem. How do we determine whom to test? Countries must set testing priorities. This requires identifying at risk populations, determining how frequently people should be tested, and developing procedures for what to do when testing is not an option. Finally, administering tests and collecting data involves a range of challenges, including the need to convince the public to get tested, standardizing the information that is collected and reported, and establishing processes for getting data to decision-makers.

[READ THE PROBLEM DESCRIPTION](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1LHALQiytFTbzU77l7WWmS2saUiLY2k-SjXKlOk0sL1Y/edit?usp=sharing) [READ THE REGIONAL REPORT](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1hgJ9YTMq9RZLl6LM6lC2z5qDJ5gFAAE7ZtmQkY5Ajb4/edit?usp=sharing) [AGENDA AND LOGISTICS](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1N91jviwqdxFPsgvKnES3u8UMZLtU2NorJ8KA5dZ7zsA/edit?usp=sharing) [EXPERTS AND PARTICIPANTS](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1ZFLCdLyl4nI6a6ZVOkJvGFJ5hnTpOU4F3_rlBsSDQMI/edit?usp=sharing)

## RECOMMENDATION

[

Pooled Testing

Governments and researchers should implement pooled testing strategies, innovating with pool design through ranking schemes or geographic schemes.

](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/recommendations/pooled-testing)

[

National Patient Identifiers

Governments should take steps toward developing a unique health identifier/national patient identifier system (UHI/NPI) that unambiguously identifies each individual and links her to her health records, including test results.

](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/recommendations/national-patient-identifiers)

[

High-risk populations

Governments should prioritize conducting tests among populations with a high probability of 1) contracting the virus; 2), spreading it to others; and 3) suffering serious consequences as a result of infection.

](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/recommendations/high-risk-populations)

[EXPLORE THE RECOMMENDATIONS](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/recommendations)

# Contact Tracing

What are the challenges associated with locating people with whom an infected person has come into contact?

[RECOMMENDATIONS MEMO](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1ZZEMqf6j1caIcjxHFZLkxxc5p_ECRB_Va6s2zOxWaG4/edit?usp=sharing) [CONFERENCE TAKEAWAYS](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1OD_vymjHw6UC5CnpcLS6qTJX9_IFRYS0I2gN9-Mx37k/edit?usp=sharing)

## DESCRIPTION

We identify seven problems associated with contact tracing. The first is establishing trust. People who have positive tests will not share information about the people with whom they have come into contact unless they trust the contract tracing personnel and organizations doing the work. Similarly, people who are contacted will be less willing to be interviewed and tested unless they trust the process. Second is determining which contacts receive the highest priority. Third, there are logistical challenges associated with locating people with whom an infected person has come into contact. Fourth, once people are contacted and asked to quarantine, it is important to support their physical and mental health needs. Fifth, recruiting, training and managing contact tracing personnel is a major challenge. Six, because contact tracing is a form of surveillance that could be abused, it is important to address the issue of privacy and protecting personal information. Finally, it is crucial to measure and evaluate the success of the contact tracing system.

[READ THE PROBLEM DESCRIPTION](https://docs.google.com/document/d/12JFEWk-QXC34Bt2JenqlSQ5566RV8YLdxh2Cxqqz0zk/edit?usp=sharing) [READ THE REGIONAL REPORT](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1KI30Ko09VTxI4P-h9Hq_92a-vtEfh7MI9_OrJrMDEh0/edit?usp=sharing) [AGENDA AND LOGISTICS](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1ajIA-WhaIFXTSBzm2SmmILe0bz9ERwyQ81eduM2zFlI/edit) [EXPERTS AND PARTICIPANTS](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1eGsqSX5tyKSIq29XVn1C1Tx6r0f1Y-i-ye8skHTysxU/edit)

## RECOMMENDATION

[

Metrics

Governments should establish and use metrics to (1) indicate thresholds where contact tracing is more or less effective as a containment and mitigation strategy; and (2) track progress and effectiveness of ongoing contact tracing programs.

](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/recommendations/metrics)

[

Interjurisdictional Coordination

Governments should increase vertical and horizontal interjurisdictional coordination by (1) incentivizing the use of interoperable or the same contact tracing platform and data collection process and (2) creating opportunities for knowledge sharing.

](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/recommendations/interjurisdictional-coordination)

[

Localization

Governments should increase public trust in contact tracing programs by ensuring the programs incorporate local knowledge and experience. Specifically, they should (1) conduct an assessment that identifies community assets; (2) partner with local community organizations to identify contact tracers; (3) conduct a public health messaging campaign to explain contact tracing; and (4) incorporate information about the local community when training the contact tracing workforce.

](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/recommendations/localization)

[EXPLORE THE RECOMMENDATIONS](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/recommendations)

# Behavioral Science and COVID

How can governments use behavioral science to support the fight against COVID-19?

[RECOMMENDATIONS MEMO](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1DzmSxBT6rqoewafUMNmdEHmjYREZ0bLnqr4JCIP1ZgE/edit?usp=sharing) [CONFERENCE TAKEAWAYS](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1vusJVfOjlWdw04VuPJ66yzhc9-slrXAXSJ_Do_YbrgE/edit?usp=sharing)

## DESCRIPTION

Successfully addressing COVID-19 pandemic requires individuals, communities, government officials, and public- and private-sector leaders to overcome and address cognitive, cultural, behavioral, and psychological barriers that are impacting or have the potential to negatively impact a coordinated response. Insights from the social and behavioral sciences provide an arsenal of tools that will help orient individual and group actions to better follow and adhere to the guidance of public health experts. There are many opportunities informed by research and evidence, including innovative approaches and new communications media, that will help improve how governments communicate with the public so as to create greater incentives for that behavior change needed to mitigate the risk of COVID-19 and to help allow for a safe and sustained reopening of societies and economies.

[READ THE PROBLEM DESCRIPTION](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1tWevzRVhcJjbidPHktAvXNWnZFXnCpB2O-2_2EK1apE/edit?usp=sharing) [READ THE REGIONAL REPORT](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1mcZx4VjYLrFdKmO9jvCKIEGpIKNtZQHYDyhVtXpZCKk/edit) [AGENDA AND LOGISTICS](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1I3Ef_eH3dydwLkrx9DwP7GoIdkxp8UK6Tp6A2WqrpoA/edit?usp=sharing) [EXPERTS AND PARTICIPANTS](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1Sqm24sXM5StmQswS4Qac3_K6KQU2fjtCVyiaJ-yKMdU/edit?usp=sharing)

## RECOMMENDATION

[

Evidence and misinformation

Combat misinformation through evidence-based, clear, and consistent messaging.

](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/recommendations/evidence-and-misinformation)

[

Community and stakeholder engagement

Engage communities and other stakeholders to make messaging strategies context specific and culturally relevant.

](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/recommendations/community-and-stakeholder-engagement)

[

Data and innovation

Use data and innovations like crowdsourcing to optimize messaging development, reach, and uptake.

](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/recommendations/data-and-innovation)

[EXPLORE THE RECOMMENDATIONS](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/recommendations)

# Supporting Marginalized and Vulnerable Populations

What are the best strategies to address disparities caused or exacerbated by the pandemic?

[RECOMMENDATIONS MEMO](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1AfYgNj7yR9NM_HkDV5ZKw8PiOhySaSeiIMwdOzkglio/edit?usp=sharing) [CONFERENCE TAKEAWAYS](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1T3Mzh9EsQrhaqJ6ZlgWF3i8p4ekAn87qp_tSMy-ka5Y/edit?usp=sharing)

## DESCRIPTION

The spread of COVID-19 has laid bare inequities and disparities in global societies. The virus is not a great equalizer, but rather has disproportionate impacts across various social, age, ethnic, socioeconomic, and cultural groups. Social determinants of health have created inequities and disparities in infection rates and severity of the outbreak in specific populations including among the elderly, indigenous, racial and ethnic minorities, the impoverished, sex workers, and other vulnerable or marginalized populations. Supporting marginalized and vulnerable populations requires policies, programs, and investments that specifically address (1) social and economic vulnerabilities, (2) physical health vulnerabilities, and (3) behavioral health vulnerabilities.

[READ THE PROBLEM DESCRIPTION](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1C8_PpxUYFsD-mmwEvo86LiVRxwafLfFF5jR2tBgH6gc/edit?usp=sharing) [READ THE REGIONAL REPORT](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1HcUbF9yljpDd-hq87VTjSitX7_5W6f8IPn1M--1i7ew/edit?usp=sharing) [AGENDA AND LOGISTICS](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1kppv5FJx2QnXyxssFKyxHcHNRjfcy0qeePQIirum_J8/edit?usp=sharing) [EXPERTS AND PARTICIPANTS](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1TQfHcbIWBQCXGGFEbfQ11Zb4ypxckypzuY4Nyj7A0AE/edit?usp=sharing)

## RECOMMENDATION

[

Improve Data Management

Improve data management (collection, storage, and analysis) processes to support evidence-driven programs and policies that identify vulnerable populations and account for their needs.

](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/recommendations/improve-data-management)

[

Establish Public-Private Partnerships

Establish Public-Private Partnerships that support vulnerable populations by filling service delivery gaps that community-based organizations, governments, and NGOs struggle to execute efficiently working on their own, while also benefiting the private institutions by providing them with financing and other resources.

](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/recommendations/establish-public-private-partnerships)

[

Engage the Public and Civil Society Organizations

Engage the public and civil society organizations to support vulnerable populations by capitalizing on existing knowledge and expertise, leveraging local assets and resources, building trust with intended beneficiaries, and strengthening the capacity of communities.

](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/recommendations/engage-the-public-and-civil-society-organizations)

[EXPLORE THE RECOMMENDATIONS](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/recommendations)

# Epidemiological monitoring and surveillance

How can governments support a sustained recovery by developing and improving epidemiological monitoring and surveillance strategies for the “new normal?

[RECOMMENDATIONS MEMO](https://docs.google.com/document/d/13uUC9vu_Kf9slV9fPlgB417kl1AWfSGrCEav_HUPeIg/edit?usp=sharing) [CONFERENCE TAKEAWAYS](https://docs.google.com/document/d/17rubdNedrR8U2XzzvqUwLXwWTeWenmmevGOqcSZ4J_w/edit?usp=sharing)

## DESCRIPTION

Policymakers, healthcare workers, businesses, and the general public lack effective, accurate, and precise ways to monitor the status of COVID-19 in their jurisdictions and communities. This problem exists up and down the crisis management continuum, from prevention to response, to recovery. Governments lack the ability to detect emerging outbreaks, monitor and surveill existing outbreaks, collaborate with other governments and stakeholders to address and surveill outbreaks, and make evidence-informed decisions about when outbreaks are no longer a threat.

[READ THE PROBLEM DESCRIPTION](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1jvmQ-jMLygoD8EfcPMOrJ1BOoaB-5-m-pMUrEUYa-7M/edit?usp=sharing) [READ THE REGIONAL REPORT](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1D8-jyCL58PT3_wyNSs1OpI1y2812tFQCiiX2858dlec/edit?usp=sharing) [AGENDA AND LOGISTICS](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1rEsMoTa3IO0TAN969Hz8K-m6aAII8eHPz6fiKqTU41w/edit?usp=sharing) [EXPERTS AND PARTICIPANTS](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1_UCvSUBPG8UjbzRVI5dGDGr9gJnRQGnKbxtLtAjYWGg/edit?usp=sharing)

## RECOMMENDATION

[

Enhance Data Collection

Enhance data collection capabilities through innovations in technologies, crowdsourcing, symptom-trackers, and partnerships.

](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/recommendations/enhance-data-collection)

[

Improve Information Infrastructure

Improve public health monitoring and surveillance information infrastructure by standardizing data formats and definitions, sharing data, and developing regulations and legislation that support public health monitoring and surveillance.

](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/recommendations/improve-information-infrastructure)

[

Increase Government Capacity

Increase government capacity to use public health monitoring and surveillance information to make policy and programmatic decisions.

](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/recommendations/increase-government-capacity)

[EXPLORE THE RECOMMENDATIONS](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/recommendations)

# Mental health and emotional wellbeing

What innovative and cost effective solutions can governments and communities implement to support the mental health needs of specific and general populations caused or exacerbated by the pandemic?

[RECOMMENDATIONS MEMO](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1DzmSxBT6rqoewafUMNmdEHmjYREZ0bLnqr4JCIP1ZgE/edit?usp=sharing) [CONFERENCE TAKEAWAYS](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1vusJVfOjlWdw04VuPJ66yzhc9-slrXAXSJ_Do_YbrgE/edit?usp=sharing)

## DESCRIPTION

Large-scale disasters are frequently accompanied by spikes in mental health issues and ripple effects such as post-traumatic stress disorder, substance abuse, anxiety, depression, behavioral disorders, child abuse, and domestic violence. These issues affect specific members of society including frontline health workers, ill individuals, families of ill individuals, essential workers, the unemployed and underemployed, and the general population who are isolated and/or quarantined. Governments are ill-equipped to respond to the mental-health consequences catalyzed by the pandemic: the large numbers of deaths, the toll of quarantine and social isolation, and the psychosocial consequences of economic recession and loss. We are looking for innovative, cost-effective ways to remedy this deficit.

[READ THE PROBLEM DESCRIPTION](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1tWevzRVhcJjbidPHktAvXNWnZFXnCpB2O-2_2EK1apE/edit?usp=sharing) [READ THE REGIONAL REPORT](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1mcZx4VjYLrFdKmO9jvCKIEGpIKNtZQHYDyhVtXpZCKk/edit) [AGENDA AND LOGISTICS](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1I3Ef_eH3dydwLkrx9DwP7GoIdkxp8UK6Tp6A2WqrpoA/edit?usp=sharing) [EXPERTS AND PARTICIPANTS](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1Sqm24sXM5StmQswS4Qac3_K6KQU2fjtCVyiaJ-yKMdU/edit?usp=sharing)

## RECOMMENDATION

[

Government capacity and regulatory environment

Improve legislative and regulatory frameworks for mental health services.

](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/recommendations/government-capacity-and-regulatory-environment)

[

Data and Technology

Use digital technologies and data to and expand access to mental health services and improve service delivery.

](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/recommendations/data-and-technology)

[

Increase provider capacity

Increase provider capacity through innovations in training opportunities and strategies to expand the workforce supply.

](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/recommendations/increase-provider-capacity)

[EXPLORE THE RECOMMENDATIONS](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/recommendations)

id: "coronavirus-smarter-crowdsourcing:recommendations/pooled-testing"
type: "GovLab policy recommendation"
title: "Pooled Testing"
url: "https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/recommendations/pooled-testing"
summary: "Governments and researchers should implement pooled testing strategies, innovating with pool design through ranking schemes or geographic schemes."
source: "The GovLab (coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org)"
licence: "Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0 International License (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)"
---

# Pooled Testing

Governments and researchers should implement pooled testing strategies, innovating with pool design through ranking schemes or geographic schemes.

- Part of: [Smarter Crowdsourcing in the Age of Coronavirus](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/), [all recommendations](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/recommendations)

## Strategy 1

Partner with academic institutions,researchers and private sector laboratories. Governments should engage the academy,research firms,and private sector laboratories to develop algorithms,testing strategies,and innovative ways to design pooled testing schemes.

- Timeframe: 1-3 Months (immediate)
- Audience: Private Sector, Academia, Government Workers
- Type: Research, Data, Partnerships
- Strategy page: https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/strategies/Partner-with-academic-institutions,researchers-and

### Actions governments should take (strategy 1)

1. Convene an [advisory panel](https://sites.google.com/tamu.edu/nets-covid/home?authuser=0) of experts with relevant skills and experience from research firms, [universities](https://isci.cl/en/covidcat/initiatives-and-reports/), and private sector laboratories
2. Commission an advisory panel to develop pooled testing strategy
3. Identify specific partners to support implementation of pooled testing strategy

### Examples from around the world (strategy 1)

1. Rwanda has enrolled scholars from multiple disciplines to [develop its pooling algorithm](https://theconversation.com/rwandas-covid-19-pool-testing-a-savvy-option-where-theres-low-viral-prevalence-141704), based on [matrix, or array testing](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/7855467/) to maximize its national pooled testing strategy and to better understand the spatial spread of COVID-19 at the national level and identify new infection hotspots. By making use of local experts, Rwanda has developed a protocol to further maximize the efficiency of pooling.

## Strategy 2

Waive regulatory barriers. Governments should consider ways to adjust regulations that restrict innovation pertaining to pooled testing schemes.

- Timeframe: 3-6 Months (medium)
- Audience: Government Workers
- Type: Policy/Legislative/Regulatory, Technology/Innovation
- Strategy page: https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/strategies/Waive-regulatory-barriers.-Governments-should-cons

### Actions governments should take (strategy 2)

1. Identify key legal and regulatory bottlenecks restricting pooled testing
2. [Review legislation and regulatory statutes that may restrict innovation pertaining to implementing pooled testing schemes](https://www.washingtonpost.com/health/what-is-pool-testing-and-how-does-it-work/2020/06/26/33eee7ea-b7e4-11ea-a510-55bf26485c93_story.html)
3. Consider policy actions, such as waivers or emergency use authorizations that will allow for temporary approvals to implement pooled testing schemes

### Examples from around the world (strategy 2)

1. The United States has issued an emergency use authorization for [Quest Diagnostics to conduct pooled testin](https://www.fda.gov/news-events/press-announcements/coronavirus-covid-19-update-fda-issues-first-emergency-authorization-sample-pooling-diagnostic)g in diagnostic testing, which will allow for pooled samples containing up to four individual swab specimens, thus bypassing normally slow regulatory procedures. [Stanford University](https://med.stanford.edu/news/all-news/2020/04/testing-pooled-samples-to-track-early-spread-of-virus.html) and the [State of Nebraska](https://www.npr.org/sections/health-shots/2020/07/06/886886255/pooling-coronavirus-tests-can-spare-scarce-supplies-but-theres-a-catch) have been conducting pooled testing since before July 2020.

## Strategy 3

Rapidly pilot pooled testing schemes. Governments should act quickly (<1 month) to pilot various pooled testing schemes such as Dorfman,Splitting,Sterret,and Matrix testing to gauge scalability and utility amongst [different contexts and populations](https://www.eurekalert.org/pub_releases/2020-04/su-vst042820.php).

- Timeframe: 1-3 Months (immediate)
- Audience: Government Workers
- Type: Policy/Legislative/Regulatory, Technology/Innovation
- Strategy page: https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/strategies/Rapidly-pilot-pooled-testing-schemes.-Governments-

### Actions governments should take (strategy 3)

1. Convene an advisory panel of experts with relevant skills and experience from research firms and universities
2. Identify ideal populations to work with on pilot testing scheme such as nursing homes, congregate living residences, or groups of healthcare workers
3. Secure partnerships with laboratories to manage the throughput of pooled tests

### Examples from around the world (strategy 3)

1. India established a [pooled testing protocol](https://www.mohfw.gov.in/pdf/GuidelineforrtPCRbasedpooledsamplingFinal.pdf) for quarantined migrant workers and international travelers which combines 25 samples at a time. The country also uses pooled testing to monitor green zones where prevalence is low. Rather than monitoring specifically vulnerable populations, India is using pooling to test groups where prevalence is perceived as being low, thus maximizing the efficiency gains from pooled testing.

## Strategy 4

Iterate learning and share best practices. Governments should contract with or perform their own evaluation of pooled testing schemes,improve on existing processes,and share best practices across jurisdictions and sectors.

- Timeframe: 6-12 Months (long)
- Audience: Government Workers
- Type: Research, Data, Technology/Innovation, Capacity Building
- Strategy page: https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/strategies/Iterate-learning-and-share-best-practices.-Governm

### Actions governments should take (strategy 4)

1. Document findings and lessons learned from pooled testing pilots
2. Share findings publicly and with relevant national and international stakeholders
3. Publish research and advocate for replication of successes within the country and in other comparator countries

### Examples from around the world (strategy 4)

1. The government of Wuhan implemented a [citywide testing drive](https://www.nytimes.com/2020/05/26/world/asia/coronavirus-wuhan-tests.html), leveraging massive resources and intensive campaigning, to test over six million people in 10 days. The aggressively high throughput in testing was only possible due to [pooling samples](https://www.livescience.com/pooled-sampling-covid19-in-wuhan-and-us-cities.html). This allowed the government to catch asymptomatic cases and prevent outbreaks, at a moment of [low prevalence](https://news.cgtn.com/news/2020-06-02/Wuhan-completes-9-89-million-COVID-19-tests-citywide--QZLbBpbAEE/index.html). Wuhan’s example shows pooled testing potential to facilitate periodic population-wide testing for a particular community.

id: "coronavirus-smarter-crowdsourcing:recommendations/national-patient-identifiers"
type: "GovLab policy recommendation"
title: "National Patient Identifiers"
url: "https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/recommendations/national-patient-identifiers"
summary: "Governments should take steps toward developing a unique health identifier/national patient identifier system (UHI/NPI) that unambiguously identifies each individual and links her to her health records, including test results."
source: "The GovLab (coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org)"
licence: "Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0 International License (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)"
---

# National Patient Identifiers

Governments should take steps toward developing a unique health identifier/national patient identifier system (UHI/NPI) that unambiguously identifies each individual and links her to her health records, including test results.

- Part of: [Smarter Crowdsourcing in the Age of Coronavirus](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/), [all recommendations](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/recommendations)

## Strategy 1

Conduct feasibility studies. Governments should appoint a group of government and external experts to conduct a feasibility study of jurisdictional and private/public context and document legislative opportunities or barriers to moving forward with a UHI/NPI system.

- Timeframe: 1-3 Months (immediate)
- Audience: Private Sector, Academia, Government Workers
- Type: Technology/Innovation, Partnerships
- Strategy page: https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/strategies/Conduct-feasibility-studies.-Governments-should-ap

### Actions governments should take (strategy 1)

1. Identify key stakeholders from government institutions, insurance companies, hospital/healthcare systems, provider networks, academic community and the public
2. Establish study timeline as less than 3 months from first meeting
3. Commission this group to develop a comprehensive assessment in the allotted time frame ensuring that the assessment includes analyses of: current system, regional differences, key stakeholders, regulatory opportunities, and recommendations for a path forward

## Strategy 2

Standardize data entry fields across existing systems. Governments should work with partners to standardize data elements across health IT systems so that data is easily shareable between systems.

- Timeframe: 1+ years (structural change)
- Audience: Private Sector, Healthcare Providers, Nonprofits
- Type: Policy/Legislative/Regulatory, Data, Partnerships
- Strategy page: https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/strategies/Standardize-data-entry-fields-across-existing-syst

### Actions governments should take (strategy 2)

1. Convene stakeholders who manage Electronic Health Record systems in the country and encourage a cost benefit analysis of current system(s)
2. Identify specific opportunities to make immediate improvements to interoperability (such as standardizing similar fields across systems)
3. Identify specific opportunities to make long-term improvements to interoperability (such as inter-system identifiers)

### Examples from around the world (strategy 2)

1. Brazil’s Unified Health System (SUS) uses a [National Healthcare Card](https://www.saude.gov.br/acoes-e-programas/cartao-nacional-de-saude), assigned to patients to keep track of medical records. The card, which has recently been digitized into an [electronic National Health identification card system](https://www.angloinfo.com/how-to/brazil/healthcare/health-system) with a personal identification number, allows healthcare providers to access a patient’s medical information anywhere in the country. This is possible due to a central database accessible from any public or private hospital within the Unified Health System network.

## Strategy 3

Develop,advocate for and pass legislation. Governments should mandate adoption of standards providing for a standard national health identifier for each individual,employer,health plan,and health care provider for use in the healthcare system.

- Timeframe: 6-12 Months (long)
- Audience: Private Sector, Academia, Healthcare Providers
- Type: Policy/Legislative/Regulatory, Data, Partnerships
- Strategy page: https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/strategies/Develop,advocate-for-and-pass-legislation.-Governm

### Actions governments should take (strategy 3)

1. Identify key legal and regulatory bottlenecks restricting adjustments to patient identifier systems
2. For regulatory barriers, consider updating regulations to better support interoperability, standardization, and the framework needed for a UHI/NPI system
3. For existing legislation, develop proposed replacement legislation and advocate for this legislation through the appropriate legislative processes and procedures

### Examples from around the world (strategy 3)

1. Estonia has one of the most [highly-developed national ID-card systems](https://e-estonia.com/solutions/e-identity/id-card/) in the world, Every citizen in Estonia has an online e-health record that can be tracked, and linked to a person’s electronic ID-card. The health records are secured with KSI Blockchain technology and are used to ensure data integrity. The information is only accessible to authorized health personnel. 99% of health data, prescription information and electronic billing in healthcare are digitized. The [Electronic Health Record](https://e-estonia.com/solutions/healthcare/) is a nationwide system that integrates data from diverse healthcare providers into a common record accessible to patients and doctors as a single electronic file. The system functions as a centralized, national database that retrieves data from various providers with different systems and presents the information into a standard format via the e-patient portal.

## Strategy 4

Adjust existing data collection processes. Governments should advance the use of regularly collected demographic data elements for patient matching and identification such as phone numbers,mailing addresses,or email addresses. This will ensure that public health authorities have up-to-date contact information when receiving reports from laboratories,hospitals,and other testing sites.

- Timeframe: 6-12 Months (long)
- Audience: Private Sector, Academia, Healthcare Providers, Government Workers
- Type: Policy/Legislative/Regulatory, Data, Partnerships
- Strategy page: https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/strategies/Adjust-existing-data-collection-processes.-Governm

### Actions governments should take (strategy 4)

1. Identify standardized demographic data fields in existing systems such as phone numbers, email addresses, home addresses, social security numbers or voting IDs
2. Develop guidance for laboratories, hospitals, and healthcare providers on how to more consistently capture these important fields
3. Rely on existing data structures where possible, such as those maintained by telecom providers, voting registries, or social security administrators

### Examples from around the world (strategy 4)

1. Estonia has one of the most [highly-developed national ID-card systems](https://e-estonia.com/solutions/e-identity/id-card/) in the world, Every citizen in Estonia has an online e-health record that can be tracked, and linked to a person’s electronic ID-card. The health records are secured with KSI Blockchain technology and are used to ensure data integrity. The information is only accessible to authorized health personnel. 99% of health data, prescription information and electronic billing in healthcare are digitized. The [Electronic Health Record](https://e-estonia.com/solutions/healthcare/) is a nationwide system that integrates data from diverse healthcare providers into a common record accessible to patients and doctors as a single electronic file. The system functions as a centralized, national database that retrieves data from various providers with different systems and presents the information into a standard format via the e-patient portal.

## Strategy 5

Establish a single organization to manage and oversee the UHI/NPI system. Governments should establish a single organization with the responsibility to oversee and advise on ways to improve patient matching and incorporate new technologies and approaches as they emerge. This organization would identify and encourage adoption of certain standards—such as on biometrics or use of smartphones—by health care organizations and technology developers.

- Timeframe: 1+ years (structural change)
- Audience: Government Workers
- Type: Policy/Legislative/Regulatory, Data, Partnerships
- Strategy page: https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/strategies/Establish-a-single-organization-to-manage-and-over

### Actions governments should take (strategy 5)

1. Appoint a special advisor on health informatics to oversee the development of identifier projects for the interim until an organization is established and functioning
2. Identify the preferred organizational affiliation of this group and how it will fit into existing government agencies and structures
3. Coordinate with international partners to learn about best practices and key steps for development and implementation

## Strategy 6

Implement a UHI/NPI system. Governments should roll out a comprehensive and single UHI/NPI system that integrates,delivers,and manages health information technology systems across all health care institutions,including the ability for individuals to access and control their own health records.

- Timeframe: 1+ years (structural change)
- Audience: Private Sector, Academia, Civil Society, Healthcare Providers, Government Workers, Nonprofits
- Type: Policy/Legislative/Regulatory, Partnerships
- Strategy page: https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/strategies/Implement-a-UHI/NPI-system.-Governments-should-rol

### Actions governments should take (strategy 6)

1. Actions listed above are all essential preconditions for this recommendation to be accomplished

### Examples from around the world (strategy 6)

1. Estonia has one of the most [highly-developed national ID-card systems](https://e-estonia.com/solutions/e-identity/id-card/) in the world, Every citizen in Estonia has an online e-health record that can be tracked, and linked to a person’s electronic ID-card. The health records are secured with KSI Blockchain technology and are used to ensure data integrity. The information is only accessible to authorized health personnel. 99% of health data, prescription information and electronic billing in healthcare are digitized. The [Electronic Health Record](https://e-estonia.com/solutions/healthcare/) is a nationwide system that integrates data from diverse healthcare providers into a common record accessible to patients and doctors as a single electronic file. The system functions as a centralized, national database that retrieves data from various providers with different systems and presents the information into a standard format via the e-patient portal.
