url: "https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/strategies/Adjust-existing-data-collection-processes.-Governm"
summary: "Adjust existing data collection processes. Governments should advance the use of regularly collected demographic data elements for patient matching and identification such as phone numbers,mailing addresses,or email addresses. This will ensure that public health authorities have up-to-date contact information when receiving reports from laboratories,hospitals,and other testing sites."
source: "The GovLab (coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org)"
licence: "Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0 International License (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)"
---

# Adjust existing data collection processes.

Adjust existing data collection processes. Governments should advance the use of regularly collected demographic data elements for patient matching and identification such as phone numbers,mailing addresses,or email addresses. This will ensure that public health authorities have up-to-date contact information when receiving reports from laboratories,hospitals,and other testing sites.

- Timeframe: 6-12 Months (long)
- Audience: Private Sector, Academia, Healthcare Providers, Government Workers
- Type: Policy/Legislative/Regulatory, Data, Partnerships
- Recommendation: [National Patient Identifiers](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/recommendations/national-patient-identifiers)
- Part of: [Smarter Crowdsourcing in the Age of Coronavirus](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/)

## Actions governments should take

1. Identify standardized demographic data fields in existing systems such as phone numbers, email addresses, home addresses, social security numbers or voting IDs
2. Develop guidance for laboratories, hospitals, and healthcare providers on how to more consistently capture these important fields
3. Rely on existing data structures where possible, such as those maintained by telecom providers, voting registries, or social security administrators

## Examples from around the world

1. Estonia has one of the most [highly-developed national ID-card systems](https://e-estonia.com/solutions/e-identity/id-card/) in the world, Every citizen in Estonia has an online e-health record that can be tracked, and linked to a person’s electronic ID-card. The health records are secured with KSI Blockchain technology and are used to ensure data integrity. The information is only accessible to authorized health personnel. 99% of health data, prescription information and electronic billing in healthcare are digitized. The [Electronic Health Record](https://e-estonia.com/solutions/healthcare/) is a nationwide system that integrates data from diverse healthcare providers into a common record accessible to patients and doctors as a single electronic file. The system functions as a centralized, national database that retrieves data from various providers with different systems and presents the information into a standard format via the e-patient portal.

id: "coronavirus-smarter-crowdsourcing:strategies/Establish-a-single-organization-to-manage-and-over"

summary: "Establish a single organization to manage and oversee the UHI/NPI system. Governments should establish a single organization with the responsibility to oversee and advise on ways to improve patient matching and incorporate new technologies and approaches as they emerge. This organization would identify and encourage adoption of certain standards—such as on biometrics or use of smartphones—by health care organizations and technology developers."
source: "The GovLab (coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org)"
licence: "Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0 International License (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)"
---

# Establish a single organization to manage and oversee the UHI/NPI system.

Establish a single organization to manage and oversee the UHI/NPI system. Governments should establish a single organization with the responsibility to oversee and advise on ways to improve patient matching and incorporate new technologies and approaches as they emerge. This organization would identify and encourage adoption of certain standards—such as on biometrics or use of smartphones—by health care organizations and technology developers.

- Timeframe: 1+ years (structural change)
- Audience: Government Workers
- Type: Policy/Legislative/Regulatory, Data, Partnerships
- Recommendation: [National Patient Identifiers](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/recommendations/national-patient-identifiers)
- Part of: [Smarter Crowdsourcing in the Age of Coronavirus](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/)

## Actions governments should take

1. Appoint a special advisor on health informatics to oversee the development of identifier projects for the interim until an organization is established and functioning
2. Identify the preferred organizational affiliation of this group and how it will fit into existing government agencies and structures
3. Coordinate with international partners to learn about best practices and key steps for development and implementation


---
id: "coronavirus-smarter-crowdsourcing:strategies/Implement-a-UHI/NPI-system.-Governments-should-rol"
type: "GovLab policy strategy"
title: "Implement a UHI/NPI system."
url: "https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/strategies/Implement-a-UHI/NPI-system.-Governments-should-rol"
summary: "Implement a UHI/NPI system. Governments should roll out a comprehensive and single UHI/NPI system that integrates,delivers,and manages health information technology systems across all health care institutions,including the ability for individuals to access and control their own health records."
source: "The GovLab (coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org)"
licence: "Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0 International License (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)"
---

# Implement a UHI/NPI system.

Implement a UHI/NPI system. Governments should roll out a comprehensive and single UHI/NPI system that integrates,delivers,and manages health information technology systems across all health care institutions,including the ability for individuals to access and control their own health records.

- Timeframe: 1+ years (structural change)
- Audience: Private Sector, Academia, Civil Society, Healthcare Providers, Government Workers, Nonprofits
- Type: Policy/Legislative/Regulatory, Partnerships
- Recommendation: [National Patient Identifiers](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/recommendations/national-patient-identifiers)
- Part of: [Smarter Crowdsourcing in the Age of Coronavirus](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/)

## Actions governments should take

1. Actions listed above are all essential preconditions for this recommendation to be accomplished

## Examples from around the world

1. Estonia has one of the most [highly-developed national ID-card systems](https://e-estonia.com/solutions/e-identity/id-card/) in the world, Every citizen in Estonia has an online e-health record that can be tracked, and linked to a person’s electronic ID-card. The health records are secured with KSI Blockchain technology and are used to ensure data integrity. The information is only accessible to authorized health personnel. 99% of health data, prescription information and electronic billing in healthcare are digitized. The [Electronic Health Record](https://e-estonia.com/solutions/healthcare/) is a nationwide system that integrates data from diverse healthcare providers into a common record accessible to patients and doctors as a single electronic file. The system functions as a centralized, national database that retrieves data from various providers with different systems and presents the information into a standard format via the e-patient portal.

id: "coronavirus-smarter-crowdsourcing:strategies/Define-high-risk-populations-who-will-receive-prio"
type: "GovLab policy strategy"
title: "Define high-risk populations who will receive prioritized testing."
url: "https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/strategies/Define-high-risk-populations-who-will-receive-prio"
summary: "Define high-risk populations who will receive prioritized testing. Governments should develop a working definition of which populations are high risk. Groups can be added to this list,but the list should identify populations that are at higher risk of contracting and having complications from COVID-19 due to physical health,behavioral health,or economic/social factors."
source: "The GovLab (coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org)"
licence: "Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0 International License (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)"
---

# Define high-risk populations who will receive prioritized testing.

Define high-risk populations who will receive prioritized testing. Governments should develop a working definition of which populations are high risk. Groups can be added to this list,but the list should identify populations that are at higher risk of contracting and having complications from COVID-19 due to physical health,behavioral health,or economic/social factors.

- Timeframe: 3-6 Months (medium)
- Audience: Civil Society, Vulnerable Populations, Essential Workers, Organized Civil Society, Nonprofits
- Type: Research, Policy/Legislative/Regulatory, Data, Partnerships, Vulnerable Populations
- Recommendation: [High-risk populations](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/recommendations/high-risk-populations)
- Part of: [Smarter Crowdsourcing in the Age of Coronavirus](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/)

## Actions governments should take

1. Review population-level data to identify high-risk groups by health-condition, profession, race/ethnicity, age, or other demographic or socio/economic factors
2. Split identified groups into those needing immediate attention and those who will be at high risk in the future (e.g. food insecure populations)
3. Ensure criteria for test allocation is transparent, explicit, simple, and consistently followed
4. Post definitions publicly to ensure transparency and accountability

## Examples from around the world

1. [Colombia’s Emergency Fund is identifying high-risk groups, including prison populations, people who have attended large gatherings, and people with known exposure to the virus, in order to test them and isolate them as needed to reduce the spread of the virus. This was done by leveraging the contact tracing methodology from Johns Hopkins University and adapting the strategies to Colombia’s social context and implementing its own Testing, Tracing, Isolation – or Pruebas, Rastreo y Aislamiento Sostenible (PRASS) program,](https://thecitypaperbogota.com/features/understanding-colombias-strategy-to-win-the-war-on-covid-19/25408)

---

# Partner with community and cultural leaders.

Partner with community and cultural leaders. Governments should conduct specific outreach and form partnerships with community and cultural leaders to 1) understand needs and concerns of specific communities and 2) amplify public health messaging encouraging surveillance,diagnostic,and screening testing.

- Timeframe: 3-6 Months (medium)
- Audience: Civil Society, Vulnerable Populations, Organized Civil Society, Nonprofits
- Type: Partnerships, Vulnerable Populations
- Recommendation: [High-risk populations](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/recommendations/high-risk-populations)
- Part of: [Smarter Crowdsourcing in the Age of Coronavirus](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/)

## Actions governments should take

1. Conduct outreach to specific community and cultural leaders to understand optimal strategies for increasing access to testing for high-risk populations in their community
2. Encourage community and cultural leaders to proactively advocate for frequent testing in their communities
3. Provide talking points or education materials to community or cultural leaders describing the benefits of testing and what actions to take depending on testing results

# Make testing free for low income or high-risk populations.

Make testing free for low income or high-risk populations. Governments should reduce barriers to testing by making testing free for specific populations,ideally for screening or surveillance purposes.

- Timeframe: 1-3 Months (immediate)
- Audience: Civil Society, Vulnerable Populations, Healthcare Providers, Organized Civil Society, Nonprofits
- Type: Policy/Legislative/Regulatory, Communications, Vulnerable Populations, Procurement/Logistics
- Recommendation: [High-risk populations](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/recommendations/high-risk-populations)
- Part of: [Smarter Crowdsourcing in the Age of Coronavirus](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/)

## Actions governments should take

1. Investigate if testing fees can be waived by government health agencies mandated to provide health services to low income individuals
2. [Consider legislative or regulatory actions that could support low-cost or free testing for identified high-risk populations](https://appropriations.house.gov/news/press-releases/house-passes-families-first-coronavirus-response-act)

# Develop and use culturally and contextually relevant communication materials for testing resources.

Develop and use culturally and contextually relevant communication materials for testing resources. Governments and public health officials should make all communication materials targeted at high-risk or vulnerable populations accessible and culturally-relevant.

- Timeframe: 1-3 Months (immediate)
- Audience: Civil Society, Vulnerable Populations, Healthcare Providers, Government Workers, Organized Civil Society, Nonprofits
- Type: Communications, Partnerships, Vulnerable Populations
- Recommendation: [High-risk populations](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/recommendations/high-risk-populations)
- Part of: [Smarter Crowdsourcing in the Age of Coronavirus](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/)

## Actions governments should take

1. [Publish a mythbusters pamphlet dispelling common rumors or misinformation about testing](https://www.who.int/emergencies/diseases/novel-coronavirus-2019/advice-for-public/myth-busters)
2. Translate all testing materials into relevant languages and ensure materials are at the appropriate literacy level to ensure accessibility
3. Provide testing information materials at testing locations in various languages, including specific information on what steps to take after receiving a specific result and how to get test results.

summary: "Rapidly conduct snapshot pooled testing among staff and residents in health and long-term care facilities,prisons,and other congregate housing facilities. Governments should conduct snapshot pooled testing to provide a baseline that will help establish subsequent testing strategies within these settings,including the frequency of testing."

# Rapidly conduct snapshot pooled testing among staff and residents in health and long-term care…

Rapidly conduct snapshot pooled testing among staff and residents in health and long-term care facilities,prisons,and other congregate housing facilities. Governments should conduct snapshot pooled testing to provide a baseline that will help establish subsequent testing strategies within these settings,including the frequency of testing.

- Timeframe: 1-3 Months (immediate)
- Audience: Vulnerable Populations, Healthcare Providers, Organized Civil Society
- Type: Policy/Legislative/Regulatory, Partnerships, Vulnerable Populations, Procurement/Logistics
- Recommendation: [High-risk populations](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/recommendations/high-risk-populations)
- Part of: [Smarter Crowdsourcing in the Age of Coronavirus](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/)

## Actions governments should take

1. Identify partners with the capacity of conducting pooled tests
2. [Develop a strategy for identifying an appropriate pool size in collaboration with the testing partner (see above section on pooled testing)](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1zKEiumAM1lKJBdijORviBacpkbE9Z63V5tHWq2f4nms/edit#heading=h.eknnyhp8ymh0)
3. Develop a plan for what will happen to staff who test positive

## Examples from around the world

1. [Seattle](https://www.nytimes.com/2020/03/13/us/coronavirus-testing-drive-through-seattle.html), [Chicago](https://www.chicago.gov/city/en/depts/cdph/provdrs/health_protection_and_response/news/2020/june/mayor-lori-lightfoot-announces-covid-19-mobile-testing-pilot-pro.html), the state of [Wisconsin](https://www.wisbusiness.com/2020/wisconsin-national-guard-conducting-mobile-testing-at-sites-around-the-state/), and other local and state governments have set up mobile testing centers to safely collect samples from healthcare workers and other high-risk or vulnerable populations.

id: "coronavirus-smarter-crowdsourcing:strategies/Ensure-adequate-testing-resources-are-available-an"
type: "GovLab policy strategy"
title: "Ensure adequate testing resources are available and accessible to high-risk communities."
url: "https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/strategies/Ensure-adequate-testing-resources-are-available-an"
summary: "Ensure adequate testing resources are available and accessible to high-risk communities. Governments should establish testing sites in communities with large numbers of high-risk individuals."
source: "The GovLab (coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org)"
licence: "Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0 International License (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)"
---

# Ensure adequate testing resources are available and accessible to high-risk communities.

Ensure adequate testing resources are available and accessible to high-risk communities. Governments should establish testing sites in communities with large numbers of high-risk individuals.

- Timeframe: 1-3 Months (immediate)
- Audience: Vulnerable Populations, Healthcare Providers, Government Workers, Organized Civil Society, Nonprofits
- Type: Policy/Legislative/Regulatory, Partnerships, Vulnerable Populations, Procurement/Logistics
- Recommendation: [High-risk populations](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/recommendations/high-risk-populations)
- Part of: [Smarter Crowdsourcing in the Age of Coronavirus](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/)

## Actions governments should take

1. Locate testing sites in areas that allow for access to populations with transportation barriers
2. Operate testing sites during specific times when populations that work non-traditional hours may have more availability, such as mornings, nights, or weekends
3. Ensure testing site design accommodates populations that may have accessibility needs including language or physical disabilities

## Examples from around the world

1. The municipal government of Lima created a [temporary shelter](https://www.radionacional.com.pe/noticias/locales/entregan-pruebas-rapidas-de-covid-19-para-personas-indigentes) for citizens in a state of abandonment that are specifically vulnerable to the spread of the virus. They did this by revamping an old historical building in 60 days and equipping it with the necessary equipment to provide food, shelter, and medical service, including testing for COVID-19.

id: "coronavirus-smarter-crowdsourcing:strategies/Reduce-barriers-to-testing-by-conducting-mobile-te"

summary: "Reduce barriers to testing by conducting mobile testing units. To address transportation limitations,non-traditional work schedules,and lack of access that may keep some communities from getting tested,governments should strategically implement mobile testing units that travel to vulnerable communities."
source: "The GovLab (coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org)"
licence: "Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0 International License (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)"
---

# Reduce barriers to testing by conducting mobile testing units.

Reduce barriers to testing by conducting mobile testing units. To address transportation limitations,non-traditional work schedules,and lack of access that may keep some communities from getting tested,governments should strategically implement mobile testing units that travel to vulnerable communities.

- Timeframe: 3-6 Months (medium)
- Audience: Civil Society, Vulnerable Populations, Healthcare Providers, Organized Civil Society, Nonprofits
- Type: Technology/Innovation, Vulnerable Populations, Procurement/Logistics
- Recommendation: [High-risk populations](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/recommendations/high-risk-populations)
- Part of: [Smarter Crowdsourcing in the Age of Coronavirus](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/)

## Actions governments should take

1. Direct mobile testing sites to locations where high-risk populations are likely to congregate
2. Operate testing sites during specific times when populations that work non-traditional hours may have more availability, such as mornings, nights, or weekends
3. Ensure testing site design accommodates populations that may have accessibility needs including language or physical disabilities

## Examples from around the world

1. [Seattle](https://www.nytimes.com/2020/03/13/us/coronavirus-testing-drive-through-seattle.html), [Chicago](https://www.chicago.gov/city/en/depts/cdph/provdrs/health_protection_and_response/news/2020/june/mayor-lori-lightfoot-announces-covid-19-mobile-testing-pilot-pro.html), the state of [Wisconsin](https://www.wisbusiness.com/2020/wisconsin-national-guard-conducting-mobile-testing-at-sites-around-the-state/), and other local and state governments have set up mobile testing centers to safely collect samples from healthcare workers and other high-risk or vulnerable populations.

id: "coronavirus-smarter-crowdsourcing:strategies/Make-raw-data-available-to-researchers,public-heal"
type: "GovLab policy strategy"
title: "Make raw data available to researchers,public health professionals and epidemiologists."
url: "https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/strategies/Make-raw-data-available-to-researchers,public-heal"
summary: "Make raw data available to researchers,public health professionals and epidemiologists. Governments should make disaggregated and,where appropriate,raw data available for modeling and epidemiological analysis. Sharing key process and outcome data with demographic and geographic identifiers allows researchers and public health officials to better predict and respond to the spread of the virus and emerging outbreaks."
source: "The GovLab (coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org)"
licence: "Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0 International License (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)"
---

# Make raw data available to researchers,public health professionals and epidemiologists.

Make raw data available to researchers,public health professionals and epidemiologists. Governments should make disaggregated and,where appropriate,raw data available for modeling and epidemiological analysis. Sharing key process and outcome data with demographic and geographic identifiers allows researchers and public health officials to better predict and respond to the spread of the virus and emerging outbreaks.

- Timeframe: 1-3 Months (immediate)
- Audience: Academia, Vulnerable Populations, Nonprofits
- Type: Research, Data, Partnerships, Vulnerable Populations
- Recommendation: [Metrics](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/recommendations/metrics)
- Part of: [Smarter Crowdsourcing in the Age of Coronavirus](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/)

## Actions governments should take

1. Establish data security protocols for sharing specific levels of de-identified or identifiable data.
2. Create processes that allow individuals with the requisite credentials (e.g. researcher, clinician, public health official) to access data easily and consistently. These individuals should be able to download the data in near real-time for analytical and modeling purposes.

## Examples from around the world

1. Taiwan took advantage of its pre-existing [National Notifiable Disease Surveillance System](https://www.liebertpub.com/doi/10.1089/hs.2016.0107) to integrate epidemiologic surveillance for COVID-19 starting in January 2020. The country built a robust contact tracing database with the information it collected from contactants, which allowed researchers to [analyze](https://jamanetwork.com/journals/jamainternalmedicine/fullarticle/2765641) the data and find correlations to estimate under which conditions contactants are more likely to contract the disease, which then could better inform contact tracing efforts


---
id: "coronavirus-smarter-crowdsourcing:strategies/Incentivize-adoption-of-standardized-process-and-o"
type: "GovLab policy strategy"
title: "Incentivize adoption of standardized process and outcome measures within jurisdictions (vertical…"
url: "https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/strategies/Incentivize-adoption-of-standardized-process-and-o"
summary: "Incentivize adoption of standardized process and outcome measures within jurisdictions (vertical standardization) and across jurisdictions (horizontal standardization) through technical assistance and cost reimbursements or cost sharing. Governments should use legislative,regulatory,and budgetary means to incentivize and/or mandate the adoption of standardized metrics across jurisdictions."
source: "The GovLab (coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org)"
licence: "Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0 International License (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)"
---

# Incentivize adoption of standardized process and outcome measures within jurisdictions (vertical…

Incentivize adoption of standardized process and outcome measures within jurisdictions (vertical standardization) and across jurisdictions (horizontal standardization) through technical assistance and cost reimbursements or cost sharing. Governments should use legislative,regulatory,and budgetary means to incentivize and/or mandate the adoption of standardized metrics across jurisdictions.

- Timeframe: 3-6 Months (medium)
- Audience: Civil Society, Healthcare Providers, Government Workers, Nonprofits
- Type: Policy/Legislative/Regulatory, Data, Partnerships
- Recommendation: [Metrics](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/recommendations/metrics)
- Part of: [Smarter Crowdsourcing in the Age of Coronavirus](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/)

## Actions governments should take

1. Conduct an analysis of existing regulatory and legislative mechanisms that may hinder or inhibit collecting, standardizing or reporting on a set of shared process and outcome metrics.
2. Issue temporary executive orders to enable collecting, standardizing and reporting on a set of shared process and outcome metrics while working toward a more durable and long term regulatory and legislative solution.
3. Advocate for and develop new or replacement legislation and regulations that codify collecting, standardizing and reporting on a set of shared process and outcome metrics for communicable diseases, including COVID-19.

## Examples from around the world

1. In [Germany](https://www.bmj.com/content/369/bmj.m2522), the national government worked to establish standards and baselines that local administration should follow - such as a minimum of contact tracers per thousand inhabitants, and a threshold for establishing lockdowns - while state health agencies were responsible for collecting and interpreting data, based on the standards set by the national government.


---
id: "coronavirus-smarter-crowdsourcing:strategies/Create-and-publish-data-dashboards-that-are-update"
type: "GovLab policy strategy"
title: "Create and publish data dashboards that are updated regularly and show progress on metrics."
url: "https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/strategies/Create-and-publish-data-dashboards-that-are-update"
summary: "Create and publish data dashboards that are updated regularly and show progress on metrics. Governments should develop a dashboard aligned with both the contact tracing platform and surveillance/reportable disease databases."
source: "The GovLab (coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org)"
licence: "Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0 International License (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)"
---

# Create and publish data dashboards that are updated regularly and show progress on metrics.

Create and publish data dashboards that are updated regularly and show progress on metrics. Governments should develop a dashboard aligned with both the contact tracing platform and surveillance/reportable disease databases.

- Timeframe: 1-3 Months (immediate)
- Audience: Civil Society, Nonprofits
- Type: Data, Communications
- Recommendation: [Metrics](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/recommendations/metrics)
- Part of: [Smarter Crowdsourcing in the Age of Coronavirus](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/)

## Actions governments should take

1. Survey available data tools that integrate with communicable disease databases and contact tracing platforms. Examples include power BI, Esri, or Tableau.
2. Fund and assign a data science team to specifically take charge of public-facing data communications, including the dashboard.
3. Maintain consistent reporting and regular updating of the dashboard to build trust and confidence with the public.

## Examples from around the world

1. Taking advantage of pre-existing data sharing frameworks and the integration of the Brazilian Unified Healthcare System (SUS), the state of Ceara has standardized and unified its health metrics and indicators in a single [portal](https://indicadores.integrasus.saude.ce.gov.br/indicadores/indicadores-coronavirus). This makes it quick and easy to compare the evolution of different metrics and evaluate measures taken. The local collection of data also insures much of it can be disaggregated by sex, gender, age, ethnicity and location.

id: "coronavirus-smarter-crowdsourcing:strategies/Commit-to-carefully-selected-metrics-that-can-be-r"

Governments should be cautious to select a small number of useful and informative metrics that can be reported on consistently,precisely,and accurately. Committing to too many metrics may lead to the inability to accurately and precisely track the data."

# Commit to carefully selected metrics that can be reported on consistently and regularly (do not select too…

Commit to carefully selected metrics that can be reported on consistently and regularly (do not select too many metrics). Governments should be cautious to select a small number of useful and informative metrics that can be reported on consistently,precisely,and accurately. Committing to too many metrics may lead to the inability to accurately and precisely track the data.

- Timeframe: 3-6 Months (medium)
- Audience: Healthcare Providers, Government Workers
- Type: Policy/Legislative/Regulatory, Data
- Recommendation: [Metrics](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/recommendations/metrics)
- Part of: [Smarter Crowdsourcing in the Age of Coronavirus](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/)

## Actions governments should take

1. Review existing databases and data collection processes and only select metrics that can be reported on consistently and regularly.

## Examples from around the world

1. [In Germany, the national government worked to establish standards and baselines that local administration should follow - such as a minimum of contact tracers per thousand inhabitants, and a threshold for establishing lockdowns - while state health agencies were responsible for collecting and interpreting data, based on the standards set by the national government.](https://www.bmj.com/content/369/bmj.m2522)

id: "coronavirus-smarter-crowdsourcing:strategies/Collaborate-with-private-and-public-sector-actors-"
type: "GovLab policy strategy"
title: "Collaborate with private and public-sector actors that have large membership across jurisdictions."

Governments should actively seek partnerships with businesses and organizations (e.g. unions) that have large numbers of employees or members based in various regions/states within the country. These businesses and organizations may be able to support interjurisdictional coordination."

# Collaborate with private and public-sector actors that have large membership across jurisdictions.

Collaborate with private and public-sector actors that have large membership across jurisdictions. Governments should actively seek partnerships with businesses and organizations (e.g. unions) that have large numbers of employees or members based in various regions/states within the country. These businesses and organizations may be able to support interjurisdictional coordination.

- Timeframe: 1-3 Months (immediate)
- Audience: Private Sector, Academia, Healthcare Providers, Government Workers, Organized Civil Society, Nonprofits
- Type: Partnerships
- Recommendation: [Interjurisdictional Coordination](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/recommendations/interjurisdictional-coordination)
- Part of: [Smarter Crowdsourcing in the Age of Coronavirus](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/)

## Actions governments should take

1. Develop criterion for inclusion in the group of large businesses and organizations (e.g. number of employees - over 100K - disaggregated by location and geographic spread)
2. Develop strict participation criteria, outlining privacy expectations and other security and ethics concerns.
3. Enlist and train representatives from these organizations and businesses as contact tracers who can report into the existing contact tracing platforms, but who will work specifically with their affiliate organization or business and its employees or members.

## Examples from around the world

1. [Through a presidential COVID-19 task force, the states of Abuja, Kano and Lagos adopted a comprehensive multisectoral approach to coordinate actions to combat the spread of COVID-19.](https://apps.who.int/iris/bitstream/handle/10665/332039/WHO-2019-nCoV-Urban_preparedness-2020.1-spa.pdf?sequence=1&isAllowed=y)

summary: "Use executive orders or other regulatory or legislative authorities to incentivize centralized platforms for contact tracing. Governments,ideally at the federal level,should mandate a single platform for contact tracing. If it is not possible at the federal level,governors of states/regions should mandate the use of a single platform within their jurisdiction."
source: "The GovLab (coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org)"
licence: "Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0 International License (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)"

# Use executive orders or other regulatory or legislative authorities to incentivize centralized platforms for…

Use executive orders or other regulatory or legislative authorities to incentivize centralized platforms for contact tracing. Governments,ideally at the federal level,should mandate a single platform for contact tracing. If it is not possible at the federal level,governors of states/regions should mandate the use of a single platform within their jurisdiction.

- Timeframe: 1-3 Months (immediate)
- Audience: Private Sector, Healthcare Providers, Government Workers
- Type: Policy/Legislative/Regulatory, Data, Technology/Innovation, Partnerships
- Recommendation: [Interjurisdictional Coordination](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/recommendations/interjurisdictional-coordination)
- Part of: [Smarter Crowdsourcing in the Age of Coronavirus](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/)

## Actions governments should take

1. Make the service free to all jurisdictions that adopt the centralized platform.
2. Ensure adequate training resources are available for onboarding all participating jurisdictions.
3. Where possible, ensure interoperability with existing communicable and reportable disease databases.

## Examples from around the world

1. [ASTHO](https://www.astho.org/default.aspx) is the national nonprofit organization representing public health agencies in the United States, the U.S. Territories, and the District of Columbia, and over 100,000 public health professionals these agencies employ. ASTHO offers various [opportunities for formal engagement and coordination](https://www.astho.org/COVID-19/Contact-Tracing-and-Disease-Intervention/) between jurisdictions (specifically states and US territories). These include, but are not limited to: (1) bi-weekly phone calls where state health officials have the opportunity to share best practices and challenges as well as learn from other invited experts from universities or federal agencies; (2) [training opportunities](https://www.astho.org/COVID-19/Making-Contact-Tracer-Training/) where states can all use a coordinated curriculum, thus increasing standard operating procedures and processes; (3) [advocating for legislation](https://www.astho.org/COVID-19/State-and-Territorial-Contact-Tracing-Legislation/) and regulations that enable coordination; and (4) writing [white papers](https://www.astho.org/ASTHOReports/COVID-19-Case-Investigation-and-Contact-Tracing-Considerations-for-Using-Digital-Technologies/07-16-20/) and [issue briefs](https://www.astho.org/COVID-19/A-National-Approach-for-Contact-Tracing/) that are shared with [policy makers in federal](https://www.centerforhealthsecurity.org/our-work/pubs_archive/pubs-pdfs/2020/200410-national-plan-to-contact-tracing.pdf) and state governments.

licence: "Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0 International License (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)"

# Use legislative or regulatory mechanisms or executive orders to enable data sharing across jurisdictions.

Use legislative or regulatory mechanisms or executive orders to enable data sharing across jurisdictions. Governments should reduce the regulatory burdens that hinder or inhibit data sharing between jurisdictions.

- Timeframe: 1-3 Months (immediate)
- Audience: Government Workers
- Type: Policy/Legislative/Regulatory, Data, Partnerships
- Recommendation: [Interjurisdictional Coordination](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/recommendations/interjurisdictional-coordination)
- Part of: [Smarter Crowdsourcing in the Age of Coronavirus](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/)

## Actions governments should take

1. Conduct an analysis of existing regulatory and legislative mechanisms that may hinder or inhibit data sharing between jurisdictions.
2. Issue temporary waivers to enable data sharing agreements while working toward a more durable and long term regulatory and legislative solution.
3. Advocate for and develop new or replacement legislation and regulations that enable data sharing between jurisdictions.

## Examples from around the world

1. [States of the European Union have agreed on common specifications and data sharing protocol to ensure that contact tracing apps from different countries can communicate. This ensures that as people travel within the Schengen area, the contact tracing app they use will communicate with others.](https://ec.europa.eu/health/sites/health/files/ehealth/docs/modelling_mobilitydata_en.pdf)

# Move towards a centralized communicable and reportable disease database and contact tracing capability.

Move towards a centralized communicable and reportable disease database and contact tracing capability. Governments should begin to invest in a federally centralized communicable and reportable disease database that will include contact tracing capabilities.

- Timeframe: 6-12 Months (long)
- Audience: Private Sector, Academia, Healthcare Providers, Government Workers
- Type: Research, Data, Technology/Innovation, Communications, Partnerships, Capacity Building
- Recommendation: [Interjurisdictional Coordination](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/recommendations/interjurisdictional-coordination)
- Part of: [Smarter Crowdsourcing in the Age of Coronavirus](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/)

## Actions governments should take

1. Identify an organization that should be the administrator of this service, ideally a nationally established center for disease control and prevention (e.g. [US CDC](https://www.cdc.gov/), [Korean CDC](https://www.cdc.go.kr/cdc_eng/), National Institutes of Public Health etc.)
2. Survey existing state or regional databases for opportunities to integrate and merge records.
3. Conduct extensive research to identify and procure the optimal contact tracing platform that can be offered to all jurisdictions within the country.
4. [Develop training program for database and contact tracing platform with options to localize training modules. (see localization)](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1ZZEMqf6j1caIcjxHFZLkxxc5p_ECRB_Va6s2zOxWaG4/edit#heading=h.a3f6xk3b5o32)

## Examples from around the world

1. [States of the European Union have agreed on common specifications and data sharing protocol to ensure that contact tracing apps from different countries can communicate. This ensures that as people travel within the Schengen area, the contact tracing app they use will communicate with others.](https://ec.europa.eu/health/sites/health/files/ehealth/docs/modelling_mobilitydata_en.pdf)

These opportunities should be extended to include researchers,epidemiologists,or non-governmental actors with contact tracking experience."
source: "The GovLab (coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org)"
licence: "Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0 International License (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)"
---

# Offer informal peer learning opportunities.

Offer informal peer learning opportunities. Governments or representative associations should coordinate informal forums or opportunities for individuals designing,implementing,and managing contact tracing programs to share ideas,challenges and best practices. These opportunities should be extended to include researchers,epidemiologists,or non-governmental actors with contact tracking experience.

- Timeframe: 1-3 Months (immediate)
- Audience: Private Sector, Academia, Government Workers
- Type: Partnerships, Capacity Building
- Recommendation: [Interjurisdictional Coordination](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/recommendations/interjurisdictional-coordination)
- Part of: [Smarter Crowdsourcing in the Age of Coronavirus](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/)

## Actions governments should take

1. Develop a database with personal contact information of individuals designing, implementing, and managing contact tracing programs.
2. Create an email listserv where individuals designing, implementing, and managing contact tracing programs can crowdsource questions to the group.
3. Create an online community or social media platform like a reddit thread or facebook group where individuals designing, implementing, and managing contact tracing programs can crowdsource questions and ideas.

## Examples from around the world

1. individuals appointed to lead contact tracing programs in New York, New Jersey, Connecticut and Pennsylvania have capitalized on informal networks and communications to improve interjurisdictional coordination. These informal communications and engagements were established through professional contacts and professional networking opportunities. One individual interviewed indicated that he was able to foster a connection between his jurisdiction and a neighboring jurisdiction because he had worked with his counterpart in a previous role. The benefits of informal networks, compared to formal networks, is that individuals were liberated to be more candid and open about experiences, successes and the challenges they faced. They were also able to strategize about the optimal ways to coordinate efforts without the restrictive environment of formal communications, meetings, or memorandums of understanding or agreements. The downside of the openness and informality of these communications is that they lacked the authority of official communications; on the other hand they influenced more formal agreements and arrangements that have made the region one of the most successful in terms of a coordinated approach to contact tracing.

licence: "Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0 International License (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)"

# Offer formal peer learning opportunities. governments or representative associations should coordinate…

Offer formal peer learning opportunities. governments or representative associations should coordinate formal and structured forums or opportunities for those designing,implementing,and managing contact tracing programs to share ideas,challenges and best practices.

- Timeframe: 1-3 Months (immediate)
- Audience: Private Sector, Academia, Government Workers
- Type: Research, Policy/Legislative/Regulatory, Data, Technology/Innovation, Partnerships, Capacity Building
- Recommendation: [Interjurisdictional Coordination](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/recommendations/interjurisdictional-coordination)
- Part of: [Smarter Crowdsourcing in the Age of Coronavirus](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/)

## Actions governments should take

1. Hold regular weekly or biweekly with individuals designing, implementing, and managing contact tracing programs.
2. Ensure meetings have a set agenda where specific topics are addressed and individual members have the opportunity to share best practices or challenges.
3. Task this group with developing recommendations and guidelines.
4. Share external resources and guidance with this network.

# Create regional partnerships and coordinating bodies.

Create regional partnerships and coordinating bodies. Governments or representative associations should establish formal and informal groups and coordinating bodies based on regional or geographic similarities,such as transportation corridors or shared geographic borders.

- Timeframe: 3-6 Months (medium)
- Audience: Government Workers
- Type: Policy/Legislative/Regulatory, Partnerships, Capacity Building
- Recommendation: [Interjurisdictional Coordination](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/recommendations/interjurisdictional-coordination)
- Part of: [Smarter Crowdsourcing in the Age of Coronavirus](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/)

## Actions governments should take

1. Define regions based on geographic or regional factors.
2. Attempt to match regions with existing regional structures used in government functions such as administrative regions, public health regions, or disaster response regions.
3. Institute informal and formal opportunities for engagement as described in the recommendations above.

## Examples from around the world

1. [States of the European Union have agreed on common specifications and data sharing protocol to ensure that contact tracing apps from different countries can communicate. This ensures that as people travel within the Schengen area, the contact tracing app they use will communicate with others.](https://ec.europa.eu/health/sites/health/files/ehealth/docs/modelling_mobilitydata_en.pdf)

# Conduct a community health assessment that identifies community assets.

Conduct a community health assessment that identifies community assets. Public health agencies responsible for conducting contact tracing should conduct an assessment of community organizations and assets that can be mobilized to support the contact tracing effort.

- Timeframe: 1-3 Months (immediate)
- Audience: Civil Society, Vulnerable Populations, Organized Civil Society, Nonprofits
- Type: Research, Data, Partnerships, Capacity Building, Vulnerable Populations
- Recommendation: [Localization](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/recommendations/localization)
- Part of: [Smarter Crowdsourcing in the Age of Coronavirus](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/)

## Actions governments should take

1. Establish formal relationships between the public health system and social service organizations
2. Identify resources that can support individuals who may need additional social support in order to isolate following a positive test result

title: "Partner with local community organizations to recruit and hire contact tracers with community-based…"

summary: "Partner with local community organizations to recruit and hire contact tracers with community-based knowledge and experience. # Partner with local community organizations to recruit and hire contact tracers with community-based…

Partner with local community organizations to recruit and hire contact tracers with community-based knowledge and experience. Governments should partner with local community organizations to identify contact tracers with the trust and knowledge of the local community. Selecting the right messenger is an important step to building trust,allowing for the cases and contacts to reveal details about who they have been in contact with and when.

- Timeframe: 1-3 Months (immediate)
- Audience: Civil Society, Vulnerable Populations, Organized Civil Society, Nonprofits
- Type: Partnerships, Capacity Building, Vulnerable Populations
- Recommendation: [Localization](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/recommendations/localization)
- Part of: [Smarter Crowdsourcing in the Age of Coronavirus](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/)

## Actions governments should take

1. Develop criteria that outlines profiles of organizations and people from the local community, that have the requisite knowledge of the community .
2. Meet with local authorities and key stakeholders (women, youths, older people) and discuss the importance of the contact tracers.
3. Establish a contract with local organizations to identify and recruit potential members of the contact tracing workforce
4. Provide financing and administrative support to allow the local community to make recruitment decisions
5. Partner with a local university or community based organization to hire, manage and/or train the contact tracing workforce
6. Develop plans for training and managing new contact tracing “employees” who are not full time employees of the public health system.

## Examples from around the world

1. [Spain hired and trained community health workers to support contact tracing efforts for tuberculosis, particularly in neighborhoods with a large number of immigrants. The government hired community health workers from countries in North Africa because they had the necessary language skills and the cultural knowledge to successfully engage with hard to reach immigrants groups. The use of these workers increased trust in the contact tracing system and improved outcomes.](https://bmcpublichealth.biomedcentral.com/articles/10.1186/1471-2458-12-158)

summary: "Conduct a public health messaging campaign explaining contact tracing. Governments should perform outreach to the public with messages about contact tracing before and while they implement telephone and in-person interviews and contact tracing. This will help the public understand why they are being contacted and what the goal of these efforts are."
source: "The GovLab (coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org)"
licence: "Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0 International License (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)"
---

# Conduct a public health messaging campaign explaining contact tracing.

Conduct a public health messaging campaign explaining contact tracing. Governments should perform outreach to the public with messages about contact tracing before and while they implement telephone and in-person interviews and contact tracing. This will help the public understand why they are being contacted and what the goal of these efforts are.

- Timeframe: 1-3 Months (immediate)
- Audience: Civil Society, Vulnerable Populations, Healthcare Providers, Essential Workers, Government Workers, Organized Civil Society, Nonprofits
- Type: Communications, Partnerships, Vulnerable Populations
- Recommendation: [Localization](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/recommendations/localization)
- Part of: [Smarter Crowdsourcing in the Age of Coronavirus](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/)

## Actions governments should take

1. Identify local people and organizations that influence local opinions
2. Offer education opportunities to community leaders.
3. Work with community groups to adapt messaging to the local culture and context
4. Contract with local influencers to develop and disseminate messages about contact tracing
5. Partner with trusted community sources to conduct regular press brieﬁngs to provide information about contact tracing
6. Develop key messages that focus on getting people to answer their phones and to engage honestly with contact tracers

## Examples from around the world

1. [During the 2014 – 2015 Ebola outbreak, thousands of community health workers were trained to serve as contact tracers. The community health workers were a crucial supplement to the existing public health workforce and helped to link the community to testing and treatment centers. The community health workers were important to the success of the program, not only because they increased the number of workers, but because they were able to help overcome the fear and lack of trust in the country’s health system during the outbreak.](https://jglobalbiosecurity.com/articles/10.31646/gbio.69/)

summary: "Incorporate communication about contact tracing into the testing program. Testing centers should inform those who are tested that they will be contacted by someone from the contact tracing program if they test positive. The testing site should provide the name of the contact tracing program and the phone number from which people will receive a call."
source: "The GovLab (coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org)"

# Incorporate communication about contact tracing into the testing program.

Incorporate communication about contact tracing into the testing program. Testing centers should inform those who are tested that they will be contacted by someone from the contact tracing program if they test positive. The testing site should provide the name of the contact tracing program and the phone number from which people will receive a call.

- Timeframe: 1-3 Months (immediate)
- Audience: Private Sector, Healthcare Providers, Organized Civil Society, Nonprofits
- Type: Communications
- Recommendation: [Localization](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/recommendations/localization)
- Part of: [Smarter Crowdsourcing in the Age of Coronavirus](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/)

## Actions governments should take

1. Inform people who are being tested that they will be contacted by people from the contact tracing program if they test positive
2. Share information about the organization that is in charge of contact tracing and the telephone number from which they should expect a call
3. Develop communications materials, such as brochures and handouts, that explain the purpose of the contact tracing program and the questions that contactants will be asked

id: "coronavirus-smarter-crowdsourcing:strategies/Incorporate-information-about-the-local-community-"
type: "GovLab policy strategy"
title: "Incorporate information about the local community when training people for the contact tracing program."
url: "https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/strategies/Incorporate-information-about-the-local-community-"
summary: "Incorporate information about the local community when training people for the contact tracing program. Governments and those designing contact tracing training programs should include specific modules that focus on the local community context,cultural practices,language considerations,and other specific considerations. The training program should also include information about how to conduct contact tracing,the workforce needs information about the local public health system,how it is organized and how it interacts with other agencies."
source: "The GovLab (coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org)"
licence: "Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0 International License (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)"
---

# Incorporate information about the local community when training people for the contact tracing program.

Incorporate information about the local community when training people for the contact tracing program. Governments and those designing contact tracing training programs should include specific modules that focus on the local community context,cultural practices,language considerations,and other specific considerations. The training program should also include information about how to conduct contact tracing,the workforce needs information about the local public health system,how it is organized and how it interacts with other agencies.

- Timeframe: 1-3 Months (immediate)
- Audience: Civil Society, Vulnerable Populations, Organized Civil Society, Nonprofits
- Type: Communications, Partnerships, Vulnerable Populations
- Recommendation: [Localization](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/recommendations/localization)
- Part of: [Smarter Crowdsourcing in the Age of Coronavirus](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/)

## Actions governments should take

1. Identify relevant features of the public health system that contact tracers need to understand
2. Identify cultural and institutional features of the community that may influence the response of the public to contact tracing, including information about any sources of distrust that may influence the community’s response to the program
3. Develop training modules that provide information about the local public health system and the local community
4. Invite members of marginalized communities to [review the script](https://www.theverge.com/2020/6/10/21285166/contact-tracing-community-partnerships-trust-coronavirus) contact tracers will use to avoid the use of language that discourage cooperation.

id: "coronavirus-smarter-crowdsourcing:strategies/Review-data-collection-processes-and-ensure-all-da"
type: "GovLab policy strategy"
title: "Review data collection processes and ensure all data systems adequately collect disaggregated data…"
url: "https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/strategies/Review-data-collection-processes-and-ensure-all-da"
summary: "Review data collection processes and ensure all data systems adequately collect disaggregated data differentiating vulnerable populations."
source: "The GovLab (coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org)"
licence: "Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0 International License (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)"
---

# Review data collection processes and ensure all data systems adequately collect disaggregated data…

Review data collection processes and ensure all data systems adequately collect disaggregated data differentiating vulnerable populations.

- Timeframe: 1-3 Months (immediate)
- Audience: Private Sector, Academia, Civil Society, Healthcare Providers, Organized Civil Society, Nonprofits
- Type: Policy/Legislative/Regulatory, Data, Technology/Innovation, Partnerships, Vulnerable Populations
- Recommendation: [Improve Data Management](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/recommendations/improve-data-management)
- Part of: [Smarter Crowdsourcing in the Age of Coronavirus](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/)

## Actions governments should take

1. List existing data collection and storage systems the government controls. A thorough audit of these systems will look both at national, subnational, and local data sources.
2. Identify opportunities to capitalize on existing data from across government ministries or health centers.
3. Review existing data collection and storage systems to ensure they capture disaggregated data by sex, age, gender, ethnicity, race, education level, socioeconomic status, and other important demographic and social factors.
4. Standardize data collection processes to ensure sex, age, race, and ethnicity are adequately captured across all systems.
5. Review each analysis to consider which populations are missing from current data collection processes and how they can be captured by existing processes.
6. Avoid missed uses of data.

## Examples from around the world

1. [The COVID-19 Sex-Disaggregated Data Tracker is a database that captures sex- and gender- disaggreagated data on COVID-19 that highlights differences in COVID-19 infection, illness and death among women and men from across the entire world. The intention of the project is to create the evidence base to identify and address gender-disparities in health outcomes and to inform gender-responsive approaches to COVID-19. and to address gender-disparities in health outcomes.](https://globalhealth5050.org/the-sex-gender-and-covid-19-project/#1587664245579-30fa0c77-7d6a)

type: "GovLab policy strategy"
title: "Build coalitions with “trust brokers” (e.g. NGOs,Civil Society Organizations,and community leaders) and…"
url: "https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/strategies/Build-coalitions-with-%E2%80%9Ctrust-brokers%E2%80%9D-(e.g.-NG"
summary: "Build coalitions with “trust brokers” (e.g. NGOs,Civil Society Organizations,and community leaders) and affected populations to co-design data collection,analysis and use processes"
source: "The GovLab (coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org)"
licence: "Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0 International License (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)"
---

# Build coalitions with “trust brokers” (e.g. NGOs,Civil Society Organizations,and community leaders) and…

Build coalitions with “trust brokers” (e.g. NGOs,Civil Society Organizations,and community leaders) and affected populations to co-design data collection,analysis and use processes

- Timeframe: 1-3 Months (immediate)
- Audience: Civil Society, Vulnerable Populations, Organized Civil Society, Nonprofits
- Type: Partnerships, Vulnerable Populations
- Recommendation: [Improve Data Management](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/recommendations/improve-data-management)
- Part of: [Smarter Crowdsourcing in the Age of Coronavirus](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/)

## Actions governments should take

1. Identify the target stakeholders. Stakeholders can be specific ages, demographics, geographic communities, language groups, etc.
2. Define the groups as specifically as possible (geographically, racially/ethnically, age breakdown, sex/gender, language groups, etc.).
3. Work with other levels of government, including sub-national, to coordinate with local actors.
4. Create a stakeholder group that includes individuals from a variety of disciplines and relevant sectors to review data management processes. These groups should include, but not be limited to, hospitals, clinicians, statisticians, social service providers, frontline-health workers, academic researchers, and community based organizations.
5. Have these stakeholders be amplifiers for helping make their constituencies more “seen” and visible to government programs through better data.
6. Ask populations for their permission to use data.

## Examples from around the world

1. [Facing the insufficiency of national ethnically disaggregated data collection protocols, the Articulation of Indigenous Peoples of Brazil has leveraged its network of smaller civil society organizations to collect better quality data from community sources.](https://emergenciaindigena.apiboficial.org/en/dados-covid-19-novo/)

id: "coronavirus-smarter-crowdsourcing:strategies/Collect-disaggregated-data-at-strategic-locations-"
type: "GovLab policy strategy"
title: "Collect disaggregated data at strategic locations and service delivery touchpoints."
url: "https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/strategies/Collect-disaggregated-data-at-strategic-locations-"
summary: "Collect disaggregated data at strategic locations and service delivery touchpoints."
source: "The GovLab (coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org)"
licence: "Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0 International License (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)"
---

# Collect disaggregated data at strategic locations and service delivery touchpoints.

Collect disaggregated data at strategic locations and service delivery touchpoints.

- Timeframe: 1-3 Months (immediate)
- Audience: Private Sector, Civil Society, Vulnerable Populations, Healthcare Providers, Essential Workers, Organized Civil Society, Nonprofits
- Type: Data, Technology/Innovation, Partnerships, Vulnerable Populations
- Recommendation: [Improve Data Management](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/recommendations/improve-data-management)
- Part of: [Smarter Crowdsourcing in the Age of Coronavirus](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/)

## Actions governments should take

1. Identify large-scale or high-volume sites serving vulnerable populations, including youth, racial minorities, women, and children.
2. Identify partners that you will need to engage to get access to these locations.
3. Identify key community leaders who can help you identify these sites or locations for collecting important information on vulnerable populations.
4. Standardize data collection processes to ensure they capture disaggregated data by sex, age, gender, ethnicity, race, education level, socioeconomic status, and other important demographic and social factors.

## Examples from around the world

1. [The city of Medellin, in Colombia, has created the Medellin me Cuida app to collect relevant data on its population. Citizens register as individuals or families, and businesses can also register. By collecting data such as address and the members of each household, and regularly screening users for symptoms, the app can give officials important contact tracing data and alert users when someone nearby has tested positive. By integrating services such as the city’s financial assistance and workers’ quarantine exemption programs into the app, Medellin has created incentives for people to register.](https://www.eltiempo.com/colombia/medellin/diferencias-entre-plataformas-medellin-me-cuida-y-bogota-cuidadora-502506https://www.eltiempo.com/colombia/medellin/diferencias-entre-plataformas-medellin-me-cuida-y-bogota-cuidadora-502506)

id: "coronavirus-smarter-crowdsourcing:strategies/Strengthen-government-capacity-to-interpret-new-an"
type: "GovLab policy strategy"
title: "Strengthen government capacity to interpret new and existing data,focusing on vulnerable populations and…"
url: "https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/strategies/Strengthen-government-capacity-to-interpret-new-an"
summary: "Strengthen government capacity to interpret new and existing data,focusing on vulnerable populations and publish data and analysis publicly."
source: "The GovLab (coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org)"
licence: "Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0 International License (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)"
---

# Strengthen government capacity to interpret new and existing data,focusing on vulnerable populations and…

Strengthen government capacity to interpret new and existing data,focusing on vulnerable populations and publish data and analysis publicly.

- Timeframe: 3-6 Months (medium)
- Audience: Private Sector, Academia, Vulnerable Populations, Government Workers
- Type: Data, Technology/Innovation, Capacity Building
- Recommendation: [Improve Data Management](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/recommendations/improve-data-management)
- Part of: [Smarter Crowdsourcing in the Age of Coronavirus](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/)

## Actions governments should take

1. Create and publish data dashboards that are updated regularly and show progress on metrics. Governments should develop a dashboard aligned with both the contact tracing platform and surveillance/reportable disease databases.
2. Survey available data tools that integrate with communicable disease databases and contact tracing platforms. Examples include power BI, Esri, or Tableau.
3. Fund and assign a data science team to specifically take charge of public-facing data communications, including the dashboard.
4. Maintain consistent reporting and regular updating of the dashboard to build trust with the public.
5. Ensure all data is disaggregated by sex, age, race, ethnicity, and other important demographic and social factors.

## Examples from around the world

1. [In Vietnam, the government partnered with PATH to improve the system by which data already being collected is registered and analyzed. By using online tools, they not only decreased the lag for case notification, but also improved data visualization, thus making it easier and more accessible to analyze existing and new data.](https://www.path.org/articles/vietnam-tuan-ngo-finds-safety-numbers/)

title: "Establish and coordinate a committee of stakeholders whose businesses,non-profits,and foundations directly…"
url: "https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/strategies/Establish-and-coordinate-a-committee-of-stakeholde"
summary: "Establish and coordinate a committee of stakeholders whose businesses,non-profits,and foundations directly serve or impact vulnerable populations to identify and address the needs of vulnerable populations."
source: "The GovLab (coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org)"
licence: "Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0 International License (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)"
---

# Establish and coordinate a committee of stakeholders whose businesses,non-profits,and foundations directly…

Establish and coordinate a committee of stakeholders whose businesses,non-profits,and foundations directly serve or impact vulnerable populations to identify and address the needs of vulnerable populations.

- Timeframe: 3-6 Months (medium)
- Audience: Private Sector, Academia, Civil Society, Vulnerable Populations, Healthcare Providers, Organized Civil Society, Nonprofits
- Type: Partnerships, Vulnerable Populations
- Recommendation: [Establish Public-Private Partnerships](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/recommendations/establish-public-private-partnerships)
- Part of: [Smarter Crowdsourcing in the Age of Coronavirus](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/)

## Actions governments should take

1. Form either sectoral or multi-sectoral commissions with diverse representations of experts as well as representatives from the communities themselves.
2. Task the committee to conduct a needs assessments and define the specific vulnerable groups needing support.
3. Appoint high-level government representatives to participate in and/or lead the commission/task force.
4. Identify specific opportunities to address immediate issues facing identified vulnerable populations.
5. Identify specific opportunities to make long-term improvements to endemic issues facing specific vulnerable populations.
6. Create formal and informal forums to connect different segments of government workers and public organizations who are working to protect the vulnerable.

## Examples from around the world

1. The [Private Sector Task Force (PSTF)](https://www.who.int/workforcealliance/knowledge/resources/privatesectorhrh_report/en/) was formed by the World Health Organization and the Global Health Workforce Alliance with the goal of understanding how the private sector can better support and lead in healthcare human resource shortages (e.g. clinicians, and public health professionals) across the globe. The Task Force identified actionable insights and put forth concrete recommendations in a [report](https://www.who.int/workforcealliance/knowledge/resources/privatesectorhrh_report/en/) that established a path towards increasing private-sector contributions to this specific public health and healthcare issue.

type: "GovLab policy strategy"
title: "Develop partnerships and engage in strategic contracts with companies who have comparative advantages or…"

summary: "Develop partnerships and engage in strategic contracts with companies who have comparative advantages or corners on specific markets like housing,transportation,diagnostic testing,and/or technology services."
source: "The GovLab (coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org)"
licence: "Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0 International License (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)"
---

# Develop partnerships and engage in strategic contracts with companies who have comparative advantages or…

Develop partnerships and engage in strategic contracts with companies who have comparative advantages or corners on specific markets like housing,transportation,diagnostic testing,and/or technology services.

- Timeframe: 3-6 Months (medium)
- Audience: Private Sector, Vulnerable Populations
- Type: Partnerships, Vulnerable Populations, Procurement/Logistics
- Recommendation: [Establish Public-Private Partnerships](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/recommendations/establish-public-private-partnerships)
- Part of: [Smarter Crowdsourcing in the Age of Coronavirus](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/)

## Actions governments should take

1. dentify key gaps in government capacity to support vulnerable populations that can be supported with private sector partnerships.
2. Conduct outreach to firms providing goods and services that fill identified gaps.
3. Coordinate with government legal advisors and procurement teams to understand the protocols and guidelines governing public-private partnerships.
4. Develop long-term retainer contracts to ensure consistent pricing consistently.
5. Ensure partnerships specifically address the needs of identified vulnerable populations and hold the contracts accountable to agreed upon measures of success.

## Examples from around the world

1. [Many state governments in Brazil have partnered with software developing company InLoco to monitor the rates of social distancing. Before the first case was confirmed in Brazil, InLoco started using mobile carrier data to track what percentage of the population is staying at home during the day, creating a social distancing index. Governments have partnered with InLoco to create solutions with this data and to analyze data at a finer spatial granularity than publicly available.](https://mapabrasileirodacovid.inloco.com.br/pt/)

id: "coronavirus-smarter-crowdsourcing:strategies/Create-a-public-commission,specifically-including-"
type: "GovLab policy strategy"
title: "Create a public commission,specifically including intended beneficiaries of the services,tasked with holding…"
url: "https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/strategies/Create-a-public-commission,specifically-including-"
summary: "Create a public commission,specifically including intended beneficiaries of the services,tasked with holding public-private partnership contracts accountable for delivering services/results through a cost effective,timely,and transparent process."
source: "The GovLab (coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org)"
licence: "Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0 International License (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)"
---

# Create a public commission,specifically including intended beneficiaries of the services,tasked with holding…

Create a public commission,specifically including intended beneficiaries of the services,tasked with holding public-private partnership contracts accountable for delivering services/results through a cost effective,timely,and transparent process.

- Timeframe: 1-3 Months (immediate)
- Audience: Civil Society, Vulnerable Populations, Organized Civil Society, Nonprofits
- Type: Partnerships, Capacity Building, Vulnerable Populations
- Recommendation: [Establish Public-Private Partnerships](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/recommendations/establish-public-private-partnerships)
- Part of: [Smarter Crowdsourcing in the Age of Coronavirus](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/)

## Actions governments should take

1. Establish a public oversight commission to oversee all public-private partnerships supporting vulnerable populations.
2. Ensure that vulnerable populations who are the target beneficiaries are key members of the oversight commission.
3. Create a public commission website so that the public can see progress with the partnership.
4. Publish all contracts, costs and results.

## Examples from around the world

1. In Malawi, the national government developed the [Public Private Partnership Commission](http://www.pppc.mw/) in 2011 which is tasked with oversight and management of all Public Private Partnerships in the country. The commission has a website that publishes a variety of information publicly, including details of all projects, information about commission members, and a full list of [PPP ongoing projects](http://www.pppc.mw/projects).
