id: "coronavirus-smarter-crowdsourcing:strategies/Partner-with-private-sector-firms-to-help-them-mee"
type: "GovLab policy strategy"
title: "Partner with private sector firms to help them meet their human resource needs by developing and…"
url: "https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/strategies/Partner-with-private-sector-firms-to-help-them-mee"
summary: "Partner with private sector firms to help them meet their human resource needs by developing and implementing retraining and reskillIng programs that help vulnerable groups adapt to the new- normal post- COVID- 19."
source: "The GovLab (coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org)"
licence: "Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0 International License (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)"
---

# Partner with private sector firms to help them meet their human resource needs by developing and…

Partner with private sector firms to help them meet their human resource needs by developing and implementing retraining and reskillIng programs that help vulnerable groups adapt to the new- normal post- COVID- 19.

- Timeframe: 6-12 Months (long)
- Audience: Private Sector, Vulnerable Populations
- Type: Partnerships, Capacity Building, Vulnerable Populations, Procurement/Logistics
- Recommendation: [Establish Public-Private Partnerships](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/recommendations/establish-public-private-partnerships)
- Part of: [Smarter Crowdsourcing in the Age of Coronavirus](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/)

## Actions governments should take

1. Conduct a rapid study identifying the hardest hit sectors, including the informal economy, and also the sectors that have seen the most growth (home delivery, etc.).
2. Engage private sector firms who have experienced large growth in their businesses and are in need of more employees.
3. Create a digital job marketplace where employers can post jobs for essential workers, the unemployed, or specific vulnerable populations.
4. Develop a training program that can be scaled and implemented to civil society organizations that focuses on how informal workers can adapt their services models to the pandemic.
5. Invest in programs that capitalize on inexpensive, proven, and widespread technologies (like smart phones) that can be used to support work opportunities such as package and goods delivery, digital payments, or other relevant goods and services.
6. Offer free online courses that teach new skills such as effective use of computer and cellphone technologies.

## Examples from around the world

1. [In Indonesia, informal workers have moved to a more digitized way of doing business with more and more SMEs registering for online marketplaces. The government also teamed up with digital companies to re-skill employees and boost their competitiveness.](https://www.thejakartapost.com/news/2020/03/20/its-official-government-digital-companies-team-up-to-launch-preemployment-card.html)

licence: "Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0 International License (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)"
---

# Work with local community leaders to tailor policy decisions to the needs of the community.

Work with local community leaders to tailor policy decisions to the needs of the community.

- Timeframe: 3-6 Months (medium)
- Audience: Civil Society, Vulnerable Populations, Organized Civil Society
- Type: Policy/Legislative/Regulatory, Partnerships, Vulnerable Populations
- Recommendation: [Engage the Public and Civil Society Organizations](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/recommendations/engage-the-public-and-civil-society-organizations)
- Part of: [Smarter Crowdsourcing in the Age of Coronavirus](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/)

## Actions governments should take

1. Form multi-sectoral commissions with diverse representations of experts as well as representatives from the communities themselves to conduct needs assessments and define the specific vulnerable groups needing support.
2. Post information online or write articles describing the process by which policies and programs are developed and how the public and specific vulnerable groups were engaged throughout the engagement.
3. Host a town hall where the public can ask questions to the experts or the government. The government can televise, live stream, or otherwise host this forum on a free and public platform to ensure it has broad reach to many segments of the population.
4. To engage specific vulnerable populations, the government should conduct targeted listening sessions and outreach to identified populations to meet them in locations where they are located and most comfortable.
5. Coordinate citizen-led messaging campaigns, where members of the target audience are the main spokespersons and public faces for that specific information campaign.

## Examples from around the world

1. [The United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR)organized a conversation with representatives of refugee-led organizations to discuss their needs and priorities as they relate to COVID-19 and how they can best be supported.](https://www.unhcr.org/2020-unhcr-annual-consultations-with-ngos/opening-conversation-high-commissioner.html)

# Partner with,fund,and support women and their families,women-owned businesses,and grassroots organizations…

Partner with,fund,and support women and their families,women-owned businesses,and grassroots organizations specifically serving women.

- Timeframe: 3-6 Months (medium)
- Audience: Vulnerable Populations, Organized Civil Society, Nonprofits
- Type: Policy/Legislative/Regulatory, Partnerships, Capacity Building, Vulnerable Populations
- Recommendation: [Engage the Public and Civil Society Organizations](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/recommendations/engage-the-public-and-civil-society-organizations)
- Part of: [Smarter Crowdsourcing in the Age of Coronavirus](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/)

## Actions governments should take

1. Where possible, provide economic support including cash, unemployment benefits, and expanded child support for vulnerable women and their families.
2. Support small and medium-sized women-owned businesses through specific government support including grants, tax-breaks, loans and funding, as well as subsidized and state-backed loans. Economic Sectors and industries where women are a large proportion of workers, including childcare, domestic work, and the food service industry.
3. Ensure that women who are informal workers are covered under economic support (e.g. don’t only issue them through established formal sectors and industries).
4. Specifically engage women-led and women-focused organizations and advocacy groups to be members of stakeholder committees and task forces.

## Examples from around the world

1. [The Asociación de Trabajadoras del Hogar, a Domicilio y Maquila (ATRAHDOM) is an organization in Guatemala that promotes labor and civil rights of women. During the pandemic, ATRAHDOM has coordinated efforts to bring relief to women domestic workers and other sectors where women are the majority of the labor force.](https://www.unwomen.org/en/news/stories/2020/9/feature-value-domestic-workers-across-latin-america)

id: "coronavirus-smarter-crowdsourcing:strategies/Detect,support-and-amplify-existing-community-led-"
type: "GovLab policy strategy"
title: "Detect,support and amplify existing community-led initiatives and solutions."
url: "https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/strategies/Detect,support-and-amplify-existing-community-led-"
summary: "Detect,support and amplify existing community-led initiatives and solutions."
source: "The GovLab (coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org)"
licence: "Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0 International License (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)"
---

# Detect,support and amplify existing community-led initiatives and solutions.

Detect,support and amplify existing community-led initiatives and solutions.

- Timeframe: 3-6 Months (medium)
- Audience: Civil Society, Vulnerable Populations, Organized Civil Society, Nonprofits
- Type: Communications, Vulnerable Populations
- Recommendation: [Engage the Public and Civil Society Organizations](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/recommendations/engage-the-public-and-civil-society-organizations)
- Part of: [Smarter Crowdsourcing in the Age of Coronavirus](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/)

## Actions governments should take

1. Identify community leaders and community groups in a given jurisdiction.
2. Conduct a community needs assessment that identifies community assets, including community organizations and assets that can be mobilized to support the response effort.
3. Establish formal relationships between the public health system and social service organizations.
4. Develop criteria that outlines profiles of organizations and people from the local community, that have the requisite knowledge of the community .
5. Meet with local authorities and key stakeholders (women, youths, older people) and discuss the importance of community-led initiatives.

## Examples from around the world

1. [During the 2014 – 2015 Ebola outbreak, thousands of community health workers were trained to serve as contact tracers. The community health workers were a crucial supplement to the existing public health workforce and helped to link the community to testing and treatment centers. The community health workers were important to the success of the program, not only because they increased the number of workers, but because they were able to help overcome the fear and lack of trust in the country’s health system during the outbreak An important lesson from the Liberia experience is to train contact tracers to pay attention to the power dynamics within society and how the daily lives of people are structured.](https://jglobalbiosecurity.com/articles/10.31646/gbio.69/)

id: "coronavirus-smarter-crowdsourcing:strategies/Crowdsource-solutions-and-expertise-from-the-publi"
type: "GovLab policy strategy"
title: "Crowdsource solutions and expertise from the public and affected populations through prizes,competitions,or…"
url: "https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/strategies/Crowdsource-solutions-and-expertise-from-the-publi"
summary: "Crowdsource solutions and expertise from the public and affected populations through prizes,competitions,or online innovation sessions."
source: "The GovLab (coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org)"
licence: "Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0 International License (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)"
---

# Crowdsource solutions and expertise from the public and affected populations through prizes,competitions,or…

Crowdsource solutions and expertise from the public and affected populations through prizes,competitions,or online innovation sessions.

- Timeframe: 3-6 Months (medium)
- Audience: Civil Society, Organized Civil Society, Nonprofits
- Type: Technology/Innovation, Communications, Capacity Building, Vulnerable Populations
- Recommendation: [Engage the Public and Civil Society Organizations](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/recommendations/engage-the-public-and-civil-society-organizations)
- Part of: [Smarter Crowdsourcing in the Age of Coronavirus](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/)

## Actions governments should take

1. Carry out an assessment, including a community mapping, to understand community structures, power dynamics, beliefs, capacities, and trusted and preferred channels of communication and sources of information.
2. Create an online challenge where teams can submit innovative solutions or ideas to solve specific problems. Offer financial, reputational, or institutional support as incentives.
3. Ensure problems that need to be solved are well defined and have a clear, articulated goal for participants to achieve
4. Host the challenge or hackathon on an open and accessible forum, such as Your Priorities.
5. If offering a prize, ensure that the prize is commensurate with the intended goal/outcome. Make sure it is culturally or otherwise appropriate for the participants of the challenge.
6. Recruit a diverse representation of participants through targeted advertising, recruitment, and outreach.

## Examples from around the world

1. [The Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT) hosted a series of challenges to empower the public to take action on the COVID-19 crisis. This “MIT COVID-19 Challenge.” MIT has run these challenges for specific audiences and specific groups of innovators, including for Latin American, African and Indian contexts.](https://covid19challenge.mit.edu/)

id: "coronavirus-smarter-crowdsourcing:strategies/Collect-epidemiological-surveillance-data-with-a-s"

title: "Collect epidemiological surveillance data with a symptom tracker or triage tool that leverages crowdsourcing…"

summary: "Collect epidemiological surveillance data with a symptom tracker or triage tool that leverages crowdsourcing and participatory surveillance."
source: "The GovLab (coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org)"
licence: "Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0 International License (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)"
---

# Collect epidemiological surveillance data with a symptom tracker or triage tool that leverages crowdsourcing…

Collect epidemiological surveillance data with a symptom tracker or triage tool that leverages crowdsourcing and participatory surveillance.

- Timeframe: 1-3 Months (immediate)
- Audience: Civil Society
- Type: Data, Technology/Innovation, Communications
- Recommendation: [Enhance Data Collection](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/recommendations/enhance-data-collection)
- Part of: [Smarter Crowdsourcing in the Age of Coronavirus](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/)

## Actions governments should take

1. Review Covid-19 symptoms and guidance from verified public health authorities like the [PAHO](https://www.paho.org/en/technical-documents-coronavirus-disease-covid-19), [WHO](https://www.who.int/emergencies/diseases/novel-coronavirus-2019/technical-guidance) or national Centers for Disease Control.
2. Identify a technology platform for participatory surveillance. For example, adapting existing smartphone-based apps and SMS platforms may be the fastest and most affordable option.
3. Conduct a review of available technologies and platforms that may already be licenced to government agencies. Survey tools like [qualtrics](https://www.qualtrics.com/lp/qualtrics-demo/?utm_source=google&utm_medium=ppc&utm_campaign=US-Brand-Qualtrics-Brand&utm_keyword=qualtrics&MatchType=e&adid=178143128566&utm_content=178143128566&adgroupid=41339289338&campaignid=755409789&AdGroup=%7BAdGroup%7D&BidMatchType=%7BBidMatchType%7D&Target=&targetid=kwd-8232955280&Device=c&devicemodel=&loc_phsyical_ms=9003967&Placement=&querystring=%7Bquerystring%7D&network=g&adposition=&GCLID=CjwKCAiAzNj9BRBDEiwAPsL0d-pnkdJzvF4z0eM1PzipWQmLI0VNl3yxv2pmFMSB_KANwgpwaSjTAhoCQBEQAvD_BwE&gclid=CjwKCAiAzNj9BRBDEiwAPsL0d-pnkdJzvF4z0eM1PzipWQmLI0VNl3yxv2pmFMSB_KANwgpwaSjTAhoCQBEQAvD_BwE), or [jotform](https://www.jotform.com/?utm_source=adwords&utm_campaign=122684001&utm_medium=cpc&adgroup=7242471681&matchtype=e&device=c&utm_term=jotform&utm_content=332697633772&extension_id=&gclid=CjwKCAiAzNj9BRBDEiwAPsL0d5c1DJmvo26VEAvnRYMRc42sr4UccvNTYMHgHCYIgUltCOge1GJXNhoC3JoQAvD_BwE), guarantee safety and security of the information and allow data to be exported and easily analyzed.
4. Develop a socialization plan that covers how the tool will be promoted and shared to encourage widespread and frequent use.
5. Consider ways to make the tool more accessible including by the graphic design, literacy level of the information, and languages that the tool is translated into.
6. Make sure that the tool offers an opt-in function to capture geographic location or approximation (e.g. zip code, census tract, etc.)
7. [Consider ways to host the tool across different platforms like a website, a smartphone app, SMS, telephone hotlines or smart paper forms.](https://shifo.org/en/solution/)
8. Consider ways to allow individuals to report symptoms at regular intervals (e.g. every day, week, etc.), by setting alerts or reminders.
9. Ensure that the tool offers concrete guidance, resources, and advice for what an individual should do given her/his personal results (e.g. if you are sick do “X”)
10. [Establish mechanisms to “push” or publicize the tool to increase use among specific and general populations. Tools like Twilio allow governments to mass message contact links via SMS.](https://www.twilio.com/sms)

## Examples from around the world

1. Governments can create an online symptom tracker that allows individuals to check and see if they are developing or have symptoms that are consistent with a COVID-19 infection. These tools create value for the person taking the assessment but also for the government who collects the data because it allows them to monitor population-level trends of infection. In New Jersey, the state’s [symptom tracker](https://covid19.nj.gov/forms/self) predicted zip code level warnings based off of ~5 percent of the population’s responses. These trackers can be promoted through SMS, targeted advertising, or other types of promotion. Additionally, they are very inexpensive to develop and maintain. The New Jersey symptom tracker was based on a similar tool in [Alberta, Canada](https://myhealth.alberta.ca/journey/covid-19/Pages/COVID-Self-Assessment.aspx).

# Invest in and promote the use of technological and digital innovations that can help collect accurate and…

Invest in and promote the use of technological and digital innovations that can help collect accurate and timely data.

- Timeframe: 1+ years (structural change)
- Audience: Private Sector, Academia
- Type: Data, Technology/Innovation, Procurement/Logistics
- Recommendation: [Enhance Data Collection](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/recommendations/enhance-data-collection)
- Part of: [Smarter Crowdsourcing in the Age of Coronavirus](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/)

## Actions governments should take

1. Promote the use of wearables (smart watches, bio stickers, etc.) and portable health technology (eg. smart thermometers) that allow individuals to report symptoms, health conditions, or comorbidities.
2. [Invest in and promote the use of technologies like smart paper, phone apps, SMS surveys, that can be used by minimally trained/skilled workers to collect data and report it into open source or centralized platforms.](https://shifo.org/en/solution/)
3. Develop a smartphone app that collects opt-in geo-spacial information that can be used for contact tracing.
4. [Pilot rapid paper-based tests when the technology is available.](https://knowablemagazine.org/article/health-disease/2020/race-develop-paper-based-tests-coronavirus)
5. Ensure technologies can integrate their data into national or centralized data systems, or open source platforms.
6. Review all tools and technologies to ensure the highest level of data security, privacy, and anonymity where relevant.

## Examples from around the world

1. “Smart paper” forms are being used in East Africa to help digitize manually collected information. “Smart Paper” are printed paper that can be filled out by hand but scanned into a computer or phone, allowing them to be digitized quickly and with great accuracy. [SHIFO](https://shifo.org/en/solution/) - a Swedish company - has developed healthcare specific forms that are being used across East Africa ([Kenya](https://doc-08-b8-docs.googleusercontent.com/docs/securesc/bm4go9cere9ic389lqpd0klor6encu4u/dnigq1dv8pr524a1d99jco1o3gcqqf3b/1604956725000/05289062938595699748/04776368802958413349/19-aTH9Rke6FCjs9Qxt_4Pl2eZdoCAnG_?authuser=0&nonce=eg8e1eo6g0eq2&user=04776368802958413349&hash=p5a3do6hqkk7f88vgmhcp7o1nj27dch4), [Uganda](https://drive.google.com/uc?id=1937yCBMc9W956Nf3Ul-jDo8JB4TfI39J), [Tanzania](https://drive.google.com/uc?id=1_3cIaQL2abN_9Xj6ip11UWQbjuBvLVEs)). This technology allows for the collection of reliable data in hard to reach areas that may not have access to digital healthcare technologies. Importantly it is very low cost.

id: "coronavirus-smarter-crowdsourcing:strategies/Partner-with-institutions-with-high-levels-of-soci"
type: "GovLab policy strategy"
title: "Partner with institutions with high levels of social engagement,trust,and access to populations to collect…"
url: "https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/strategies/Partner-with-institutions-with-high-levels-of-soci"
summary: "Partner with institutions with high levels of social engagement,trust,and access to populations to collect information and implement public health monitoring and surveillance systems."
source: "The GovLab (coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org)"
licence: "Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0 International License (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)"
---

# Partner with institutions with high levels of social engagement,trust,and access to populations to collect…

Partner with institutions with high levels of social engagement,trust,and access to populations to collect information and implement public health monitoring and surveillance systems.

- Timeframe: 1-3 Months (immediate)
- Audience: Private Sector, Academia, Civil Society, Healthcare Providers, Organized Civil Society, Nonprofits
- Type: Data, Technology/Innovation, Partnerships, Capacity Building
- Recommendation: [Enhance Data Collection](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/recommendations/enhance-data-collection)
- Part of: [Smarter Crowdsourcing in the Age of Coronavirus](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/)

## Actions governments should take

1. Identify institutions with high levels of social engagement and/or community trust to potentially partner with on surveillance systems. These may include institutions like elementary or secondary schools, religious institutions, sports organizations, large employers like factories, and importantly primary care and public health facilities.
2. Build relationships with key individuals in these institutions who will be leading the work internally to that institution. Make sure that this point of contact is empowered to make decisions and provide internal leadership to the partnership.
3. Where possible, invest in capacity building and training for data collection amongst the staff persons in these institutions.
4. Conduct training of trainers (TOT).
5. Create an online course or asynchronous learning module that explains the fundamentals of the requested collaboration, including instructions on how to use the appropriate softwares, apps, or other data collection technologies.

## Examples from around the world

1. [Public health officials should use social surveillance systems that capitalize on institutions that populations already trust (e.g. schools, churches/religious institutions, community centers, etc.). In Mexico, the Directorate of Economic and Social Benefits at the Mexican Institute of Social Security (IMSS) is using data from employers across the country that indicates when workers are out sick or absent. This data is used to forecast where outbreaks may occur.](https://www.thelancet.com/journals/lanpub/article/PIIS2468-2667(20)30157-2/fulltext)

id: "coronavirus-smarter-crowdsourcing:strategies/Develop-standard-definitions,structures,and-variab"
type: "GovLab policy strategy"
title: "Develop standard definitions,structures,and variables for key public health monitoring and surveillance…"
url: "https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/strategies/Develop-standard-definitions,structures,and-variab"
summary: "Develop standard definitions,structures,and variables for key public health monitoring and surveillance health data."
source: "The GovLab (coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org)"
licence: "Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0 International License (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)"
---

# Develop standard definitions,structures,and variables for key public health monitoring and surveillance…

Develop standard definitions,structures,and variables for key public health monitoring and surveillance health data.

- Timeframe: 3-6 Months (medium)
- Audience: Academia
- Type: Research, Policy/Legislative/Regulatory, Data, Partnerships, Capacity Building
- Recommendation: [Improve Information Infrastructure](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/recommendations/improve-information-infrastructure)
- Part of: [Smarter Crowdsourcing in the Age of Coronavirus](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/)

## Actions governments should take

1. Convene stakeholders who manage Electronic Health Record (EHR) systems and other epidemiological data systems across the country and encourage a crosswalk of the current system(s) to identify potentials for standardizations.
2. Identify specific opportunities to make immediate improvements to interoperability (such as standardizing similar fields across systems) and long-term improvements to interoperability (such as inter-system identifiers) .
3. Identify standardizable demographic data fields in existing systems such as phone numbers, email addresses, home addresses, social security numbers or voting IDs. Rely on existing data structures where possible, such as those maintained by telecom providers, voting registries, or social security administrators.
4. Develop guidance for laboratories, hospitals, and healthcare providers on how to more consistently capture these important fields.
5. Hold a workshop with key stakeholders to develop standard definitions, structures and variables.
6. Develop a parallel system to collect the data that fixes the data infrastructure issues and that is compatible with existing instruments of data collection. This system should be opt-in and voluntary but it can be promoted through incentives.
7. Incentivize adoption of standardized process and outcome measures within jurisdictions (vertical standardization) and across jurisdictions (horizontal standardization) through technical assistance and cost reimbursements or cost sharing.

## Examples from around the world

1. Estonia has one of the most [highly-developed national ID-card systems](https://e-estonia.com/solutions/e-identity/id-card/) in the world. Every citizen in Estonia has an online e-health record that can be tracked, and linked to a person’s electronic ID-card. The health records are secured with KSI Blockchain technology and are used to ensure data integrity. The information is only accessible to authorized health personnel. 99% of health data, prescription information and electronic billing in healthcare are digitized. The [Electronic Health Record](https://e-estonia.com/solutions/healthcare/) is a nationwide system that integrates data from diverse healthcare providers into a common record accessible to patients and doctors as a single electronic file. The system functions as a centralized, national database that retrieves data from various providers with different systems and presents the information into a standard format via the e-patient portal.

id: "coronavirus-smarter-crowdsourcing:strategies/Promote-and-use-open-source-and-simple-tools-for-d"
type: "GovLab policy strategy"
title: "Promote and use open source and simple tools for data sharing between and among stakeholders."
url: "https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/strategies/Promote-and-use-open-source-and-simple-tools-for-d"
summary: "Promote and use open source and simple tools for data sharing between and among stakeholders."
source: "The GovLab (coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org)"
licence: "Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0 International License (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)"
---

# Promote and use open source and simple tools for data sharing between and among stakeholders.

Promote and use open source and simple tools for data sharing between and among stakeholders.

- Timeframe: 3-6 Months (medium)
- Audience: Private Sector, Academia, Civil Society, Healthcare Providers, Government Workers, Organized Civil Society, Nonprofits
- Type: Policy/Legislative/Regulatory, Data, Technology/Innovation, Capacity Building
- Recommendation: [Improve Information Infrastructure](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/recommendations/improve-information-infrastructure)
- Part of: [Smarter Crowdsourcing in the Age of Coronavirus](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/)

## Actions governments should take

1. Review policies that govern and restrict the storage and sharing of health information.
2. Set up an online, open repository for national surveillance data that provides timely reports in machine-readable format.
3. Offer informal peer learning opportunities where governments or representative associations coordinate informal forums or opportunities for individuals designing, implementing, and managing public health monitoring and surveillance programs to share ideas, challenges and best practices. These opportunities should be extended to include researchers, epidemiologists, or non-governmental actors.
4. Offer formal peer learning opportunities where governments or representative associations coordinate formal and structured forums or opportunities for those designing, implementing, and managing public health monitoring and surveillance programs to share ideas, challenges and best practices.
5. Publish open datasets to encourage participation of multiple research groups; use scientific peer-review as a system of checks and balances ensuring research quality.
6. Establish a code of conduct for research using public surveillance datasets.
7. Establish a single organization with the responsibility to oversee and advise on ways to improve data sharing and incorporate new technologies and approaches as they emerge.
8. Capitalize on existing databases or registers maintained by specific government agencies (such as social security, post service, or census data) to bolster existing public health monitoring and surveillance data systems.
9. Integrate these databases into the public health monitoring and surveillance data systems or contact tracing platform to increase ability for contact tracers to reach individuals confirmed as COVID-19 positive or identified as contacts of COVID-19 positive cases.
10. [Develop and use a data governance playbook for epidemic response and building broad commitment to it (see GovLab Zika/MBD Report)](https://zika.smartercrowdsourcing.org/en/files/smarter-crowdsouring-for-zika-and-other-mosquito-borne-diseases.pdf)

## Examples from around the world

1. The European Bioinformatics Institute launched the [Covid-19 Data Portal](https://www.covid19dataportal.org/) in collaboration with multiple European partners. The portal is funded by the European Union to allow researchers and healthcare professionals to [submit, share, and access publicly available data on COVID-19](https://coronavirusexplained.ukri.org/en/article/vdt0011/) in order to assist in developing diagnostic tools, treatment and a vaccine.

id: "coronavirus-smarter-crowdsourcing:strategies/Develop-and-advocate-for-a-legislative-framework-f"
type: "GovLab policy strategy"
title: "Develop and advocate for a legislative framework for public health monitoring and surveillance health data."
url: "https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/strategies/Develop-and-advocate-for-a-legislative-framework-f"
summary: "Develop and advocate for a legislative framework for public health monitoring and surveillance health data."
source: "The GovLab (coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org)"
licence: "Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0 International License (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)"
---

# Develop and advocate for a legislative framework for public health monitoring and surveillance health data.

Develop and advocate for a legislative framework for public health monitoring and surveillance health data.

- Timeframe: 6-12 Months (long)
- Audience: Government Workers
- Type: Policy/Legislative/Regulatory, Data
- Recommendation: [Improve Information Infrastructure](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/recommendations/improve-information-infrastructure)
- Part of: [Smarter Crowdsourcing in the Age of Coronavirus](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/)

## Actions governments should take

1. Conduct an analysis of existing regulatory and legislative mechanisms that may hinder or inhibit collecting, standardizing or sharing data.
2. Issue temporary executive orders to enable data sharing while working toward a more durable and long-term regulatory and legislative solution. Use executive orders or other regulatory or legislative authorities to incentivize data sharing.
3. Advocate for and develop new or replacement legislation and regulations that codify processes and mechanisms for open data sharing and interoperability of data structures and systems.
4. Pass legislation or regulations that allows for controlled access to clinical data and the secondary use of that data.
5. Use an executive order to direct all agencies to open the data they have related to measuring the impact of COVID, including both public health and economic data and data relevant to measuring impact on minority and vulnerable populations.
6. issue a statistical policy directive establishing any needed public health data standards to improve national, local and non-governmental reporting of information necessary to respond to the coronavirus pandemic. Any new data standard or directive should apply consensus, voluntary standards to the extent practicable.
7. Adopt a standard that is used to transport the data when you don’t know who the recipient is. Examples of data sharing models include [HL7 - FHIR](https://www.hl7.org/) and [N3C](https://covid.cd2h.org/) (N3C Data Enclave is a secure platform through which the harmonized clinical data provided by our contributing members is stored).
8. For existing legislation, develop proposed replacement legislation and advocate for this legislation through the appropriate legislative processes and procedures.
9. Reduce the regulatory burdens that hinder or inhibit data sharing between jurisdictions.

## Examples from around the world

1. [The Operational Framework for Mutual Aid Requests (OFMAR) is a mechanism that allows Provincial/Territorial (PT) governments to identify and share healthcare assets and professionals throughout jurisdictions. It has also established procedures to conduct emergency registration of healthcare professionals in other jurisdictions to ensure they are available to travel to the areas where they are most needed.](https://www.canada.ca/en/public-health/services/diseases/2019-novel-coronavirus-infection/health-professionals/covid-19-pandemic-guidance-health-care-sector.html)


---
id: "coronavirus-smarter-crowdsourcing:strategies/Increase-government-capacity-to-use-public-health-"
type: "GovLab policy strategy"
title: "Increase government capacity to use public health monitoring and surveillance data by training government…"
url: "https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/strategies/Increase-government-capacity-to-use-public-health-"
summary: "Increase government capacity to use public health monitoring and surveillance data by training government workers in data science and partnering with data scientists."
source: "The GovLab (coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org)"
licence: "Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0 International License (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)"
---

# Increase government capacity to use public health monitoring and surveillance data by training government…

Increase government capacity to use public health monitoring and surveillance data by training government workers in data science and partnering with data scientists.

- Timeframe: 6-12 Months (long)
- Audience: Private Sector, Academia, Government Workers
- Type: Data, Technology/Innovation, Capacity Building
- Recommendation: [Increase Government Capacity](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/recommendations/increase-government-capacity)
- Part of: [Smarter Crowdsourcing in the Age of Coronavirus](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/)

## Actions governments should take

1. Allocate funds from current training budgets to fully or partially fund employees to attend existing data science programs offered by local or international universities.
2. Partner with universities or research institutions to develop training programs for government staff and workers.
3. Partner with universities or research institutions for secondments of subject matter experts who can fill capacity gaps while training programs are being established.
4. Identify cultural and institutional features of the community that may influence the quality of monitoring data, including information about any sources of distrust that may influence the community’s response to the program. Include specific modules or materials on accounting for these biases in the data.
5. Ensure that the partnership is led by a government counterpart that is passionate to get things done and who has access to resources and technical knowledge of data analysis.
6. Partner with a data science company by carrying out a bidding process to contract an external provider. In-house data expertise is necessary to define the scope of the project, evaluate the proposals and manage the project.
7. Include modules that teach government workers to design, maintain, and publish data dashboards that are updated regularly and show progress on metrics.
8. Fund and assign a data science team to specifically take charge of public-facing data communications, including data dashboards.
9. Conduct training at the local level and/or support the hiring of health IT specialists and health informatics specialists.

## Examples from around the world

1. [n Central America, the RECAINSA is working very closely with COMISCA (https://www.sica.int/comisca/) to provide training for epidemiologists and to strengthen the Government's capacity to collect and use data efficiently.](https://www.sica.int/comisca)

id: "coronavirus-smarter-crowdsourcing:strategies/Develop,use,and-refine-multiple-predictive-models-"
type: "GovLab policy strategy"
title: "Develop,use,and refine multiple predictive models to help with pandemic planning,preparedness,and response."
url: "https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/strategies/Develop,use,and-refine-multiple-predictive-models-"
summary: "Develop,use,and refine multiple predictive models to help with pandemic planning,preparedness,and response."
source: "The GovLab (coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org)"
licence: "Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0 International License (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)"
---

# Develop,use,and refine multiple predictive models to help with pandemic planning,preparedness,and response.

Develop,use,and refine multiple predictive models to help with pandemic planning,preparedness,and response.

- Timeframe: 1-3 Months (immediate)
- Audience: Academia, Government Workers
- Type: Research, Data, Technology/Innovation
- Recommendation: [Increase Government Capacity](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/recommendations/increase-government-capacity)
- Part of: [Smarter Crowdsourcing in the Age of Coronavirus](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/)

## Actions governments should take

1. Estimate preparedness of and potential impact on healthcare infrastructure.
2. Use open-source data to predict and model viral spread.
3. Be creative in finding new data sources such as government hotline data.
4. Get the public to collect and contribute data. Citizen participation can be leveraged in data collection. When the community’s contribution is built on trust, data collection can be increased and improved, especially if the community can see a correlation to useful public services provided as a result.
5. Establish public-private data partnerships (data collaboratives) with the private sector. Data sources that illustrate human movement are especially valuable and those can be sourced from telephone companies. Data sources that illustrate behavior are also valuable and these can be sourced from search engine companies.
6. Incentivize engagement with the data-science community through prize-backed challenges. Use challenges to rapidly develop alternative predictive models and leverage outside expertise.
7. Assess the risks and biases inherent in the data in order to plan for and mitigate unintended consequences.
8. Increase data analytics capacity of public health officials in partnership with research institutions and universities through training and other knowledge transfer opportunities.

## Examples from around the world

1. Open source models like [Facebook AI](https://ai.facebook.com/blog/using-ai-to-help-health-experts-address-the-covid-19-pandemic/) model or the [UPenn Chime Model](https://oto.med.upenn.edu/2020/03/31/covid-19-hospital-impact-model-for-epidemics-chime/) can be used to predict impacts on specific populations, such as elderly populations or those living in [long term care facilities](https://jamanetwork.com/journals/jama/article-abstract/2767062). They have also been used to 1) predict cases and deaths, 2) predict hospital level demand, 3) support bed capacity planning, 4) predict peak estimation, 5) support PPE estimation, and 6) estimate second wave modeling.

id: "coronavirus-smarter-crowdsourcing:strategies/Create-a-COVID-19-“war-room”,emergency-operati"
type: "GovLab policy strategy"
title: "Create a COVID-19 “war room”,emergency operation center,or nerve center that centralizes data and decision…"
url: "https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/strategies/Create-a-COVID-19-%E2%80%9Cwar-room%E2%80%9D,emergency-operati"
summary: "Create a COVID-19 “war room”,emergency operation center,or nerve center that centralizes data and decision making."
source: "The GovLab (coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org)"
licence: "Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0 International License (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)"
---

# Create a COVID-19 “war room”,emergency operation center,or nerve center that centralizes data and decision…

Create a COVID-19 “war room”,emergency operation center,or nerve center that centralizes data and decision making.

- Timeframe: 3-6 Months (medium)
- Audience: Government Workers
- Type: Policy/Legislative/Regulatory, Data, Technology/Innovation, Communications, Capacity Building, Procurement/Logistics
- Recommendation: [Increase Government Capacity](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/recommendations/increase-government-capacity)
- Part of: [Smarter Crowdsourcing in the Age of Coronavirus](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/)

## Actions governments should take

1. Ensure that the nerve center follows an established management system such as the National Incident Management System (NIMS) in the USA or the Incident Coordination System in Australia.
2. Develop a data linkage environment or platform that rapidly and confidentially supports data matching, de-identification, and use. This platform/environment should integrate data from different sources and allow officials to access it for decision making through a user-friendly interfaces.
3. Establish clear and written responsibilities and expectations for nerve center staff based on their experience and expertise. Functions should include leadership and management, operations, information management, logistics, media, security, administration, and technology.
4. Standardize an organizational structure based on clear top-down command and control with all the commanding positions arranged hierarchically.
5. Continually update and manage contact information for all officials and staff so that no gaps in service occur.
6. Conduct exercises to evaluate the nerve center ability to respond to specific and general public health emergencies.
7. Maintain situational awareness by integrating multiple data streams from government databases, healthcare surveillance systems, mass media, online social media, hotlines, and other data sources.
8. Strengthen information management by developing methods for risk detection and assessment.

## Examples from around the world

1. [Mckinsey & Company has developed resources for setting up a “minimum viable nerve center” that is designed to solve (1) inadeate discovery - or the “depths, extent and velocity of the crisis”; (2) poor decision making; (3) constrained solution design; and (4) delivery failure. Their model is applicable to individual organizations and also to governments.](https://www.mckinsey.com/business-functions/risk/our-insights/responding-to-coronavirus-the-minimum-viable-nerve-center)

id: "coronavirus-smarter-crowdsourcing:strategies/Create-a-legal-framework-to-regulate-and-fund-ment"
type: "GovLab policy strategy"
title: "Create a legal framework to regulate and fund mental health priorities"
url: "https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/strategies/Create-a-legal-framework-to-regulate-and-fund-ment"
summary: "Create a legal framework to regulate and fund mental health priorities"
source: "The GovLab (coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org)"
licence: "Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0 International License (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)"
---

# Create a legal framework to regulate and fund mental health priorities

Create a legal framework to regulate and fund mental health priorities

- Timeframe: 1+ years (structural change)
- Audience: Vulnerable Populations
- Type: Partnerships, Vulnerable Populations
- Recommendation: [Government capacity and regulatory environment](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/recommendations/government-capacity-and-regulatory-environment)
- Part of: [Smarter Crowdsourcing in the Age of Coronavirus](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/)

## Actions governments should take

1. Review existing provisions regulating and legislating mental health services in the jurisdiction
2. Advocate for economic stimuli to include appropriations for mental health services and providers.
3. Reduce regulatory requirements for face to face service provision, thus allowing service provision to capitalize on remote technologies like telemedicine or hotlines.
4. Reduce regulatory requirements for licensure or credentialing across jurisdictions thus allowing providers to practice via technologies in jurisdictions where they are not licensed.
5. Review legal regulations for controlled substances like methadone, antidepressants, or other key medications used to treat depression, substance abuse, and other mental health issues.
6. Consider means of reducing barriers for patients to access these essential medications while minimizing risks for in-person visits and risks of transmission of the virus.
7. Include provisions for paid sick leave for people who have COVID-19 symptoms, need to quarantine, or are caring for children or ill family to reduce stress and financial burdens of the illness.
8. Include provisions that mandate the coverage of mental health and behavioral health services at the same level as other physical health services or treatments.
9. Include provisions that provide financing for mental health services, including specific details on how services that support marginalized or poor populations will be funded and prioritized.

## Examples from around the world

1. Ireland established the Mental Health Act in 2001 sets out legal procedures for the admissions and treatment of mental health patients, it also established a [Mental health commission](https://www.mhcirl.ie/About_Us/) which is incharge of ensuring and promoting good practices in the delivery of mental health services. Currently, the Commission was tasked with developing a [risk assessment framework](https://www.mhcirl.ie/for_H_Prof/MHC%20Covid-19%20Risk%20Assessment%20Framework/) as part of enhanced public health measures to ensure the proper disease management of COVID-19 and to work with national and regional governance to assess and support their mental health services. Given that a legal framework already existed it allowed for the [Emergency Measures in the Public Interest Covid-19](http://www.irishstatutebook.ie/eli/2020/act/2/enacted/en/html) Act to be passed in 2020.

id: "coronavirus-smarter-crowdsourcing:strategies/Create-a-national-mental-health-plan-to-guide-the-"
type: "GovLab policy strategy"
title: "Create a national mental health plan to guide the implementation of the resulting legislation and regulations"
url: "https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/strategies/Create-a-national-mental-health-plan-to-guide-the-"
summary: "Create a national mental health plan to guide the implementation of the resulting legislation and regulations"
source: "The GovLab (coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org)"
licence: "Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0 International License (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)"
---

# Create a national mental health plan to guide the implementation of the resulting legislation and regulations

Create a national mental health plan to guide the implementation of the resulting legislation and regulations

- Timeframe: 3-6 Months (medium)
- Audience: Government Workers
- Type: Research, Policy/Legislative/Regulatory, Capacity Building
- Recommendation: [Government capacity and regulatory environment](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/recommendations/government-capacity-and-regulatory-environment)
- Part of: [Smarter Crowdsourcing in the Age of Coronavirus](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/)

## Actions governments should take

1. Identify national or subnational priorities, goals, and/or objectives pertaining to prevention, screening, assessment, and treatment of mental disorders and behavioral conditions.
2. Articulate them clearly in the plan, with specific timelines and indicators to measure these outcomes and objectives.
3. Consider the needs of populations that may be experiencing disparities in access, treatment and mental health outcomes. For example, racial/ethnic minority populations, poor populations, and rural communities may be less likely to have access to care and more likely to receive lower-quality care.
4. Ensure that implementation plans integrate monitoring, evaluation and learning opportunities into all aspects of new work.
5. Take advantage of natural experiments that have resulted from responses to the COVID-19 crisis, such as quasi-experimental studies of mental health outcomes based on changes in use of telehealth, hotlines, apps, or other innovations that have become prevalent during the pandemic.
6. Ensure the plan outlines such areas as reimbursement rules, patient eligibility criteria for programs, rules regarding what types of services are permitted in certain settings, accreditation requirements, and what types of waivers may be appropriate in certain situations.

## Examples from around the world

1. [Chile established the National Mental Health Plan 2017-2025 that sets out guidelines for the implementation of a community model of mental health care and that also considers the establishment of a legal framework in order to establish a Mental Health law in the upcoming years,](https://www.minsal.cl/wp-content/uploads/2017/12/PDF-PLAN-NACIONAL-SALUD-MENTAL-2017-A-2025.-7-dic-2017.pdf)

id: "coronavirus-smarter-crowdsourcing:strategies/Promote-public-policies-and-interventions-that-pri"
type: "GovLab policy strategy"
title: "Promote public policies and interventions that prioritize mental health services for healthcare workers and…"
url: "https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/strategies/Promote-public-policies-and-interventions-that-pri"
summary: "Promote public policies and interventions that prioritize mental health services for healthcare workers and frontline personnel"
source: "The GovLab (coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org)"
licence: "Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0 International License (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)"
---

# Promote public policies and interventions that prioritize mental health services for healthcare workers and…

Promote public policies and interventions that prioritize mental health services for healthcare workers and frontline personnel

- Timeframe: 1-3 Months (immediate)
- Audience: Healthcare Providers, Essential Workers, Organized Civil Society, Nonprofits
- Type: Policy/Legislative/Regulatory, Communications
- Recommendation: [Government capacity and regulatory environment](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/recommendations/government-capacity-and-regulatory-environment)
- Part of: [Smarter Crowdsourcing in the Age of Coronavirus](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/)

## Actions governments should take

1. Develop, fund, and implement specific hotlines and telehealth services that provide expedited services for healthcare workers and frontline personnel.
2. Conduct studies and research that specifically consider the impacts of COVID-19 on the mental health and emotional wellbeing of healthcare workers and essential workers.
3. Establish government programs to support the mental health needs of healthcare workers and essential workers, prioritizing them as a vulnerable or high risk group.
4. Encourage hospitals and healthcare organizations to conduct regular screenings for mental health problems in frontline and healthcare workers.
5. Train workers peer to identify burnout and offer informal support and counseling to their peers.
6. Encourage hospitals and healthcare organizations to provide mental health resource materials for their staff and offer training in stress management.

## Examples from around the world

1. To address the large numbers of healthcare workers suffering mental health disorders, [Penn Medicine](https://www.pennmedicine.org/) (Penn), in collaboration with UnitedHealth Group, created [COBALT](https://www.penncobalt.com/)— “a digital platform that offers immediate access to mental health support for health care workers during this critical time.” The system connects employees in need to mental health and wellness content, live groups, and individual virtual support all online. The platform employs targeted assessments to direct specific content to individuals presenting specific conditions and to triage users to specific types and modalities of support. The platform makes available resources including “resilience coaches, psychotherapists, and psychiatrists, as well as podcasts, articles, mindfulness sessions, and other group support.”

type: "GovLab policy strategy"
title: "Use technology to bridge access gaps and reach individuals who cannot access treatment due to…"
url: "https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/strategies/Use-technology-to-bridge-access-gaps-and-reach-ind"
summary: "Use technology to bridge access gaps and reach individuals who cannot access treatment due to cost,location,language,or other barriers."
source: "The GovLab (coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org)"
licence: "Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0 International License (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)"
---

# Use technology to bridge access gaps and reach individuals who cannot access treatment due to…

Use technology to bridge access gaps and reach individuals who cannot access treatment due to cost,location,language,or other barriers.

- Timeframe: 1-3 Months (immediate)
- Audience: Private Sector, Academia, Civil Society, Vulnerable Populations, Healthcare Providers, Organized Civil Society, Nonprofits
- Type: Technology/Innovation, Communications, Procurement/Logistics
- Recommendation: [Data and Technology](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/recommendations/data-and-technology)
- Part of: [Smarter Crowdsourcing in the Age of Coronavirus](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/)

## Actions governments should take

1. Use technology to augment existing processes and procedures, rather than creating digital first replacements from scratch.
2. Analyze what processes and tools already exist and how they can be adapted and strengthened with technology. Use the existing technology, equipment and tools specifically in the LAC context, and reinforce them with technology.
3. Adapt existing telemedicine or other medical care practices for mental health, with an approach that mental health disorders --- especially the more common ones -- can be for a large part approached as most other medical conditions and have evidence based treatments that work for a large part of patients.
4. Ensure that investments in technology to provide better mental health services focus on the care providers offer, not only on the tech they use to do so. Focusing on particular platforms or software may result in suboptimal tech that doesn’t fit the use case. Focus on the goals providers want to achieve, and then identify the technologies that can best achieve them.
5. Ensure that investments in new technologies to support mental health services are accompanied with underlying investments in the service provision itself, including governance, training, operations, funding, and workforce development. Technologies are useless unless people know how to use them both as providers and users.
6. Create and staff a mental health telephone hotline. Ensure that the telephone hotline is offered in various languages and is staffed by providers trained on cultural competencies and contexts of the targeted populations.
7. Promote the widespread use of video sessions and telemedicine to allow providers to work with patients remotely.
8. Consider waivers that would enable the use of video conferencing or video chat technologies for mental health care services.
9. Create cost sharing arrangements for proprietary technologies or endorse open source technologies, apps, or platforms that providers can use with existing or new patients without having to themselves invest heavily in new capital costs.
10. Partner with 3rd party vendors (like digital mental health apps such as [headspace](https://www.headspace.com/?utm_source=google&utm_medium=cpc&utm_campaign=1919439341&utm_content=68065219102&utm_term=409649586657&headspace&gclid=CjwKCAiA7939BRBMEiwA-hX5J_ELhZInSt8LaAdKqFk9K7-IusjH0KOmhmhq_1ianGvvMWfCSk970BoC3t0QAvD_BwE) and [calm](https://www.calm.com/)) to distribute reduced cost or free apps and digitied services that patients and individuals can use asynchronously and independently.
11. Create specific interventions for rural populations by providing facilitative technologies like phone lines, broadband connections, smartphones and telehealth services. Couple technology provision with training on how to use those technologies.
12. Monitor for inequities in engagement with new technologies across groups with limited access to smartphones or the internet.
13. [Invest in and promote the use of technologies like smart paper, phone apps, SMS surveys, that can be used by minimally trained/skilled workers to collect data and report it into open source or centralized platforms.](https://shifo.org/en/solution/)
14. Invest in technologies that help reduce wait times and scheduling issues.

## Examples from around the world

1. [AI for Good](https://www.aiforgood.co.uk/) - a company that uses ethical technology and AI-powered solutions to address social issues - released [rAInbow](https://www.hirainbow.org/) in 2018. [rAInbow](https://www.hirainbow.org/) is a chatbot that helps users understand their relationships, what is healthy and what is not. It also provides resources that users can access to get more support. Nearly 20,000 unique users have interacted with this chatbot.

id: "coronavirus-smarter-crowdsourcing:strategies/Improve-mental-health-data-collection-and-use-thro"
type: "GovLab policy strategy"
title: "Improve mental health data collection and use through technologies"
url: "https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/strategies/Improve-mental-health-data-collection-and-use-thro"
summary: "Improve mental health data collection and use through technologies"
source: "The GovLab (coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org)"
licence: "Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0 International License (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)"
---

# Improve mental health data collection and use through technologies

Improve mental health data collection and use through technologies

- Timeframe: 3-6 Months (medium)
- Audience: Healthcare Providers
- Type: Data, Technology/Innovation, Capacity Building
- Recommendation: [Data and Technology](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/recommendations/data-and-technology)
- Part of: [Smarter Crowdsourcing in the Age of Coronavirus](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/)

## Actions governments should take

1. [Invest in and promote the use of technologies like smart paper, phone apps, SMS surveys, that can be used by minimally trained/skilled workers to collect data and report it into open source or centralized platforms.](https://shifo.org/en/solution/)
2. Digitize mental health screenings by transitioning paper process to digital formats on tablets or smartphones
3. Develop an app for managing and tracking patients exercise, habits, and use of prescribed medications.
4. [Consider how different digital platforms like websites, smartphone apps, SMS, telephone hotlines or smart paper forms can be used to support data collection for mental health or behavioral health conditions.](https://shifo.org/en/solution/)
5. Consider ways to allow patients to report symptoms or conditions at regular intervals (e.g. every day, week, etc.), by setting alerts or reminders.
6. Consider ways to crowdsource data collection through the internet or smartphones, for example, by creating a means where individuals can flag associates that may be suffering from depression, suicidal ideation or who may be victims of domestic abuse.
7. Ensure that platforms that collect patient data offers concrete guidance, resources, and advice for what an individual should do given her/his reported symptoms (e.g. if you are thinking of hurting yourself call “XXX-XXXX”)

## Examples from around the world

1. [A smartphone application called MONARCA, allows the collection of data on bipolar disorder by allowing patients to self-monitor symptoms of bipolar disorder and to connect through an interactive feedback loop with clinicians.](https://bmjopen.bmj.com/content/3/7/e003353.long)

id: "coronavirus-smarter-crowdsourcing:strategies/Use-technology-to-train-community-health-workers-a"
type: "GovLab policy strategy"
title: "Use technology to train community health workers and other healthcare providers who may have no experience…"
url: "https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/strategies/Use-technology-to-train-community-health-workers-a"
summary: "Use technology to train community health workers and other healthcare providers who may have no experience in mental healthcare and mental first aid"
source: "The GovLab (coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org)"
licence: "Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0 International License (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)"
---

# Use technology to train community health workers and other healthcare providers who may have no experience…

Use technology to train community health workers and other healthcare providers who may have no experience in mental healthcare and mental first aid

- Timeframe: 1-3 Months (immediate)
- Audience: Healthcare Providers, Organized Civil Society, Nonprofits
- Type: Technology/Innovation, Partnerships, Capacity Building
- Recommendation: [Increase provider capacity](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/recommendations/increase-provider-capacity)
- Part of: [Smarter Crowdsourcing in the Age of Coronavirus](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/)

## Actions governments should take

1. Shortages of specialists in the settings that need support can be addressed by guiding non-specialists in a step-by-step way to deliver an evidence based intervention. Step-by-step guidelines ensure adherence to guidelines and also reduces stress on the provider.
2. Create repositories of existing mental health educational resources for people to use.
3. Translating resources from other languages is less resource and time intensive than creating them from scratch. Many resources are written in English but have not been translated into Spanish or other languages.
4. Identify cost effective means of translating existing resources from English or other languages into Spanish or Portuguese. Examples can include using students or bilingual individuals.
5. Adapt available open source manuals on how to adapt digital technology to train community health workers on psychological assessments, such as those provided by the digital training website of the Healthy Activity Program (HAP).

## Examples from around the world

1. The Faculties of Medicine, Psychology and Nursing of the Pontificia Universidad Javeriana have created [a platform and strategy](https://www.javeriana.edu.co/mentescolectivas/) that offers support and mental health counseling to Colombians of legal age. The platform allows individuals seeking support to select their preferred form of communication which include chat services, email, or phone calls. A group of student volunteers, [trained in mental health issues](https://www.javeriana.edu.co/mentescolectivas/), then reach out and speak with the individuals to listen and also recommend tools that can support an individual’s well-being. Pontificia Universidad Javeriana has also created [an information hub](https://www.javeriana.edu.co/mentalpuntodeapoyo/?page_id=2010) with tips and resources for individuals to proactively protect their mental health.

title: "Engage cross-sectoral partners to utilize available mental health resources and increase the supply of…"

summary: "Engage cross-sectoral partners to utilize available mental health resources and increase the supply of providers"
source: "The GovLab (coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org)"
licence: "Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0 International License (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)"
---

# Engage cross-sectoral partners to utilize available mental health resources and increase the supply of…

Engage cross-sectoral partners to utilize available mental health resources and increase the supply of providers

- Timeframe: 3-6 Months (medium)
- Audience: Civil Society, Vulnerable Populations, Healthcare Providers, Government Workers, Organized Civil Society, Nonprofits
- Type: Technology/Innovation, Partnerships, Capacity Building
- Recommendation: [Increase provider capacity](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/recommendations/increase-provider-capacity)
- Part of: [Smarter Crowdsourcing in the Age of Coronavirus](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/)

## Actions governments should take

1. Work with local community leaders to identify mental health gaps and needs of their community.
2. Form multi-sectoral commissions with diverse representations of experts to conduct needs assessments and define the mental health needs of specific groups and to identify the best strategies to reach those needing support.
3. Partner with universities and colleges to recruit psychology, psychiatry and nursing students to offer care via telehealth and other technologies.
4. Partner with schools, workplaces, community centers, religious institutions and other cultural institutions to offer training opportunities to build the capacity of non-specialist staff persons in these institutions.
5. Engage these institutions to socialize available resources and direct their constituents, members, students, employees etc. to those available resources.
6. Conduct training of trainers (TOT) for basic psychological first aid courses and make training available to non-specialists and laypersons in communities and community institutions.
7. Ensure that schools, community centers, religious institutions and other cultural centers are aware of and provide support resources to their constituent members.
8. Create an online course or asynchronous learning module that explains the fundamentals of the requested collaboration, including instructions on how to use the appropriate softwares, apps, or other data collection technologies.
9. Identify neighboring jurisdictions or external supplies of providers that have capacity to support provision of services via tech-enabled services (e.g. phone lines, telemedicine, etc.).

## Examples from around the world

1. [In Colombia, health workers from Pontificia Universidad Javeriana have created repositories of existing mental health educational resources for people to use. Translating resources from other languages (English tends to be the richest) is less resource and time intensive than creating these resources from scratch.](https://www.javeriana.edu.co/mentalpuntodeapoyo/)

id: "coronavirus-smarter-crowdsourcing:strategies/Governments-should-keep-messaging-consistent-and-e"
type: "GovLab policy strategy"
title: "Governments should keep messaging consistent and explain changes when they are made."
url: "https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/strategies/Governments-should-keep-messaging-consistent-and-e"
summary: "Governments should keep messaging consistent and explain changes when they are made."
source: "The GovLab (coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org)"
licence: "Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0 International License (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)"
---

# Governments should keep messaging consistent and explain changes when they are made.

Governments should keep messaging consistent and explain changes when they are made.

- Timeframe: 1-3 Months (immediate)
- Type: Communications
- Recommendation: [Evidence and misinformation](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/recommendations/evidence-and-misinformation)
- Part of: [Smarter Crowdsourcing in the Age of Coronavirus](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/)

## Actions governments should take

1. Review guidance at predictable and publicized intervals. If guidance needs to change, communicate why it needs to change.
2. Prioritize communications from trusted leaders at a consistent time and in a consistent format.
3. [Use credible sources and use them consistently (see strategy on evidence and credibility)](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1DzmSxBT6rqoewafUMNmdEHmjYREZ0bLnqr4JCIP1ZgE/edit#heading=h.g2kgkwezebr7)
4. Be transparent and communicate openly about the frequency of when guidance is reviewed. This will prime the population that guidance may change based on the changing circumstances.
5. Acknowledge that the message has been updated if the public health guidance changes.
6. Designate a spokesperson to establish credibility, convey confidence and maintain consistency.

## Examples from around the world

1. [In Ireland the prime minister appointed a communications expert to coordinate public messaging. The government also delivered a booklet with basic information on COVID-19 to every household thus ensuring everyone received the same consistent and reliable information on symptoms and instructions on how to self-isolate. The Irish Health Minister, serves as a consistent and reliable spokesperson, briefing the public every night at 7pm on relevant COVID-19 information and answers questions via facebook.](https://theconversation.com/clear-consistent-health-messaging-critical-to-stemming-epidemics-and-limiting-coronavirus-deaths-134529)

id: "coronavirus-smarter-crowdsourcing:strategies/Governments-and-policy-makers-should-make"

title: "Governments and policy makers should make sure the messages they are promoting are scientifically accurate…"
url: "https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/strategies/Governments-and-policy-makers-should-make"
summary: "Governments and policy makers should make sure the messages they are promoting are scientifically accurate and informed by evidence and base all messaging on credible levels of evidence and review levels of evidence. The public is more likely to trust messages coming from credible sources"
source: "The GovLab (coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org)"
licence: "Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0 International License (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)"
---

# Governments and policy makers should make sure the messages they are promoting are scientifically accurate…

Governments and policy makers should make sure the messages they are promoting are scientifically accurate and informed by evidence and base all messaging on credible levels of evidence and review levels of evidence. The public is more likely to trust messages coming from credible sources

- Timeframe: 1-3 Months (immediate)
- Type: Data, Communications
- Recommendation: [Evidence and misinformation](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/recommendations/evidence-and-misinformation)
- Part of: [Smarter Crowdsourcing in the Age of Coronavirus](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/)

## Actions governments should take

1. Identify trusted sources such as public health authorities, clinicians, scientists or international sources (e.g. World Health Organization - WHO).
2. Ensure messaging cites/acknowledges this credible source so the public is aware of where the information is coming from.
3. Build credibility of specific sources by citing them consistently and correctly.
4. Avoid politicizing evidence and scientific facts

## Examples from around the world

1. [Germany’s Chancellor Angela Merkel uses science and clear evidence-based explanations of disease modelling when she discusses the pandemic and pathways toward recovery.](https://www.theguardian.com/world/2020/apr/16/angela-merkel-draws-on-science-background-in-covid-19-explainer-lockdown-exit)


---
id: "coronavirus-smarter-crowdsourcing:strategies/Governments-should-track-rumors-and-misinformation"
type: "GovLab policy strategy"
title: "Governments should track rumors and misinformation campaigns to ensure that communities are not acting on…"
url: "https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/strategies/Governments-should-track-rumors-and-misinformation"
summary: "Governments should track rumors and misinformation campaigns to ensure that communities are not acting on incorrect public health guidance."
source: "The GovLab (coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org)"
licence: "Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0 International License (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)"
---

# Governments should track rumors and misinformation campaigns to ensure that communities are not acting on…

Governments should track rumors and misinformation campaigns to ensure that communities are not acting on incorrect public health guidance.

- Timeframe: 1-3 Months (immediate)
- Audience: Academia
- Type: Data, Communications
- Recommendation: [Evidence and misinformation](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/recommendations/evidence-and-misinformation)
- Part of: [Smarter Crowdsourcing in the Age of Coronavirus](https://coronavirus.smartercrowdsourcing.org/)

## Actions governments should take

1. [Create crowdsourced initiatives to spot and debunk misinformation and promote advertised channels where citizens can report misinformation or false information. This can be through a mobile app, hotline, SMS or WhatsAPP, or a website.](https://www.pnas.org/content/116/7/2521)
2. Conduct targeted outreach to specific communities or community leaders to understand rumors that may be proliferating in their communities.
3. [Create a rumor management and tracking tool.](https://covid19communicationnetwork.org/covid19resource/creating-a-real-time-rumor-management-system-technical-brief/)
4. Engage groups providing similar services to [Public Editor](https://www.publiceditor.io/) or [Politifact](https://www.politifact.com/) to help flag false information in the news, online, and coming from politicians.
5. [Promote evidenced-based sources, like Ask a Scientist, where people can seek independently verified and scientific information when they have questions about specific rumors.](https://covid19.fas.org/)
6. [Work with tech companies to flag false information on social media platforms, including twitter flags.](https://www.cnn.com/2020/10/11/tech/twitter-flags-donald-trump-tweet-coronavirus/index.html)
7. [Don’t “fan the flames” by elevating misinformation as you address it.](https://www.rockefellerfoundation.org/wp-content/uploads/2020/10/CovidTestingTracing_Handbook.pdf)
8. [Engage influencers, TV stations, radio stations or other trusted sources to advertise which rumors have been disproven.](https://www.thebodypro.com/article/covid-19-pandemic-turns-doctors-into-social-media-influencers)
9. [Track messages responding to rumors through the use of a engagement tool such as bit.ly](https://bit.ly/)
10. [Ensure officials are transparent and accountable to the public to increase credibility of official messaging](https://www.cdc.gov/eis/field-epi-manual/chapters/Communicating-Investigation.html)

## Examples from around the world

1. The UK government partnered with the WHO to create the “ [Stop the spread](https://www.who.int/news-room/feature-stories/detail/countering-misinformation-about-covid-19)” campaign which aims to raise awareness about misinformation. The campaign is being featured on BBC World News and BBC.com and the UK government is providing partner governments with a toolkit of the campaign assets for use in their countries. The UK government also set up [a rapid response](https://www.bbc.com/news/technology-52086284) team to crackdown on fake and misleading information circulating online on COVID-19 and has a [don’t feed the beast](https://sharechecklist.gov.uk/) campaign which provides 5 steps on how to identify fake news.
